# Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack v3.18.6-2607 Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) Enterprise Distributed Application Service User Guide 20260828

prise Distributed Application Serv ice (EDAS)?

## What is Enterprise

**Distributed Application**

**Service (EDAS)?**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) is a cloud-native Platform as a Service (PaaS) platform that lets you manage applications and microservices. EDAS provides fullstack solutions for developing, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining applications. It supports microservice frameworks such as Spring Cloud and Dubbo to help you easily deploy microservice applications to the cloud.

**Application hosting**

Application hosting is a model where developers host applications with a service provider (SP) instead of on their own servers. After you develop an application, you can host it on EDAS.

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Multiple underlying server choices | EDAS seamlessly integrates with Elastic Compute Service (ECS) and Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK). Select an ECS cluster or an ACK cluster as needed. |
| Multiple release methods | Deploy applications using the console, API, command-line interface (CLI), or software development kits (SDKs). You can also use the Cloud Toolkit plug-in to automate application deployment. |
| Multiple deployment modes | Deploy applications using WAR packages, JAR packages, or images. |
| Application management | EDAS provides full lifecycle management for applications. You can publish, start, stop, scale out, scale in, roll back, and delete applications. This lets you easily maintain thousands of application instances. |
| Application monitoring | Monitoring: EDAS monitors the health of IaaS layer resources and application services in real time. This helps you quickly troubleshoot errors. You can also activate Application Real-Time Monitoring Service (ARMS) for advanced monitoring. Logs: View the run logs of an application on an instance without logging on to the instance. If an application error occurs, check the logs to troubleshoot the error. Alerting: If resources are overused, EDAS sends text messages or emails to specified contacts so they can promptly address the issues. |
| Auto Scaling | Auto Scaling helps you handle traffic bursts. EDAS automatically scales out applications to a reasonable level to handle traffic bursts and scales them in after the traffic subsides. This effectively reduces resource costs. |

**Microservices**

prise Distributed Application Serv ice (EDAS)? Unlike traditional monolithic application architectures, the microservices model divides an application into multiple core features. Each feature can be an independent service that is built, deployed, and managed by an independent team. Services run independently and do not affect each other if errors occur. Microservices make applications easier to scale and faster to develop. This accelerates innovation and shortens the release cycle for new features. EDAS provides a comprehensive solution for developing, deploying, and governing microservice applications.

**Application Development**

EDAS supports microservice applications developed using Spring Cloud, Apache Dubbo, and High-speed Service Framework (HSF). You can deploy applications that use these frameworks to EDAS without modifying any code or configurations. For more information, see Application development overview.

| Spring Cloud | Apache Dubbo | HSF |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Cloud overview Implement service registration and discovery Implement load balancing Implement configuration management | Dubbo overview Develop Dubbo microservice applications with Spring Boot | Introduction to HSF Start the lightweight configuration and registration center Asynchronous invocations Generalized calls |

**Microservice Administration**

EDAS provides the following service administration features for Java and multilingual applications: Java Spring Cloud: Supports service query, trace query, outlier ejection, and service authentication. Dubbo: Supports service query, trace query, outlier ejection, and service authentication. HSF: Supports service query, trace query, service grouping, and end-to-end traffic shaping. Multilingual: Supports service query and service authentication.

**PaaS platform for cloud-native applications**

Cloud-native applications are applications that are developed to run on the cloud for optimal performance. These applications can take full advantage of the cloud. In the cloud-native era, PaaS platforms can be deployed on the infrastructure to become an integral part of the cloud. EDAS is a PaaS platform that lets you manage applications and microservices.

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Configuration management | EDAS is integrated with Application Configuration Management (ACM). In EDAS, use ACM to centrally manage and push application configurations. You can also use namespaces to isolate and synchronize configurations between different environments. |
| Permission management | Account system with main accounts and RAM users: This system lets you build relationships between a main account and RAM users in EDAS based on the departments, teams, and projects of your enterprise. ECS resources are also organized based on these account relationships. This simplifies resource allocation. Role and permission control: Application lifecycle management often involves different roles, such as development, O&M, and instance resources. Different roles have access to different application management operations. EDAS provides a role and permission control mechanism that lets you assign custom roles to different accounts and grant corresponding permissions to the roles. Service authentication: This feature ensures the reliability and security of each distributed call. Strict service authentication is implemented at all phases such as service registration, service subscription, and service invocation. |

ba Cloud Application Server

## What is Alibaba Cloud

**Application Server**

Alibaba Cloud Application Server (AliEE) is enterprise-grade JavaEE application server software for building and deploying enterprise applications. It provides a scalable, reliable, and secure platform, supporting various application development languages and protocols, such as Java, J2EE, Web Services, SOAP, HTTP, and HTTPS. Alibaba Cloud Application Server runs on multiple operating systems, including Windows and Linux, and supports various server chips.

**Important**

Currently, Alibaba Cloud Application Server (AliEE) only provides runtime environment support within the EDAS product in its initial phase.

**Features**

**Domestic Adaptation**

With the rapid development of global information technology, domestic adaptation has become a crucial part of national strategy. Alibaba Cloud Application Server fully considers domestic adaptation requirements from its initial design. Chip adaptation: Supports various chips (such as X86/Arm), including all domestic chip architectures deployable by Apsara Stack, ensuring efficient operation on different hardware platforms. Server compatibility: Works closely with domestic server brands (such as Kunpeng and Phytium), ensuring optimal system compatibility and performance. Operating system compatibility: Compatible with mainstream domestic operating systems, including Anolis, AliyunLinux2/3, Kylin, and UnionTech. Database support: Compatible with mainstream domestic databases (PolarDB, OceanBase, Dameng, and Kingbase), providing stable and reliable data storage and processing capabilities.

**Microservices Interconnection**

With the increasing popularity of the microservices model, Alibaba Cloud Application Server leverages EDAS's native capabilities, providing comprehensive microservice administration support by default for applications hosted on Alibaba Cloud Application Server: Protocol support: Supports various microservice communication protocols, such as RESTful, gRPC, and Dubbo, ensuring smooth communication between different services. Link monitoring: Integrates microservice link monitoring tools, monitoring service call links in real time, and promptly detecting and resolving issues. Service discovery: Provides a service discovery mechanism, automatically registering and discovering service instances, simplifying mutual discovery and communication between services.

**Cloud-Native Container Support**

Cloud-native technology is core to modern enterprise IT architecture. Alibaba Cloud Application Server supports cloud-native container scenarios by default: ba Cloud Application Server Containerized deployment: Supports container technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, and Helm charts, simplifying application deployment and management. It also supports direct deployment of application packages (Jar/War/Ear) to container environments. Dynamic runtime adaptation: In container scenarios, applications automatically detect exact resources (such as CPU/Mem) within the container during startup. Supports external application configuration: Externalize application runtime configurations to ConfigMap and Nacos, preventing configuration loss when a pod is destroyed. Auto Scaling: Supports automatic scaling, dynamically adjusting resources based on application load, and improving resource utilization.

**Capabilities**

**JakartaEE 8 Support**

Alibaba Cloud Application Server strictly adheres to Jakarta EE 8 specifications, providing the following capabilities: Web services: Supports Web service technologies such as Servlet, JSP, and WebSocket, meeting Web application development requirements. Enterprise services: Provides enterprise services such as EJB, JPA, and JTA, supporting complex business logic and data management. Message Service: Integrates JMS, supporting asynchronous message processing, and improving application response speed and reliability.

**Deep Integration with Cloud Products and Services**

As a cloud product, Alibaba Cloud Application Server leverages cloud capabilities by default, providing more specialized and comprehensive support, including the following: Cloud resource integration: Leveraging Platform as a Service (PaaS) capabilities on the cloud, Alibaba Cloud Application Server deeply integrates with products such as cloud hosts and Server Load Balancer, enabling resources and binding Server Load Balancer by default to expose services externally. Cloud service integration: Integrates with cloud PaaS services such as Microservices Engine, application monitoring, databases, and Message Service by default, enabling applicationcentric, one-stop management and use of PaaS service resources. Cloud security: Integrates cloud Security Services (such as WAF), ensuring enterprise data security and compliance.

**Large-Scale Cluster Management**

In large-scale distributed systems, cluster management is key to ensuring stable system operation: Cluster deployment: Supports large-scale cluster deployment, with the ability to manage ultra-large-scale clusters. While providing high availability, it supports dynamic load balancing between nodes. Cluster monitoring: Integrates cluster monitoring tools, monitoring cluster status in real time, and promptly detecting and resolving issues. Cluster expansion: Supports online cluster expansion, allowing you to add nodes without downtime and improving system scalability.

**Scenarios**

**Domestic Replacement for Existing Application Servers**

ba Cloud Application Server For enterprises requiring domestic hardware and software support, Alibaba Cloud Application Server provides comprehensive domestic adaptation, completely replacing products from foreign vendors such as WebSphere and WebLogic, ensuring the secure and reliable operation of enterprise information systems.

**Microservices Model Transformation**

For enterprises transforming to a microservices model, Alibaba Cloud Application Server provides microservices interconnection capabilities, helping enterprises build flexible and scalable microservices models. This ensures smooth migration of business during architecture refactoring.

**Cloud-Native Architecture Transformation**

For enterprises needing to upgrade to a cloud-native architecture, Alibaba Cloud Application Server provides complete containerization support, enabling enterprises to quickly develop and deploy cloud-native applications.

### Select an environment to

**deploy applications**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) supports deploying applications in Elastic Compute Service (ECS) clusters and Kubernetes clusters. Both environments can host your applications, but they offer different features. If you are choosing a technology or migrating your architecture and are unsure which environment to use, this topic compares the two environments and provides suggestions to help you make a decision.

**Introduction to deployment environments**

EDAS provides two cluster deployment environments for applications: ECS and Kubernetes. Both ECS and Kubernetes clusters support hosting, service administration, and observability for Java applications that use the Spring Cloud, Dubbo, or High-Speed Service Framework (HSF) microservice frameworks. Only Kubernetes clusters support hosting, service administration, and observability for multi-language applications. Additionally, these two deployment environments have different requirements for your applications and technology stack. The application management capabilities that EDAS provides also differ between the two environments.

**Suggestions for selecting a deployment environment**

In most cases, we recommend that you use the Kubernetes environment to deploy applications. EDAS is deeply integrated with Alibaba Cloud Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) and provides a rich set of application management features to help you achieve higher resource utilization. Choose the environment that is right for your scenario.

| Scenario | Environment |
|---|---|
| Your applications are container images or non-Java applications. You require high-density deployment or deploying multiple instances of an application on a single node. You want to use Kubernetes features or tools, such as kubectl, for management. | Kubernetes Environment |
| You have many non-containerized applications. The ECS environment is better for non-containerized applications because it makes it easier to reuse existing application O&M systems. Applications that require exceptional single-instance performance and stability. | ECS Environment |

**Note**

If your applications are already deployed in an ECS environment and you want to use the advanced features of Kubernetes, you can migrate the applications to a Kubernetes environment.

**Comparison of application hosting features**

The following table compares the features of the ECS and Kubernetes environments. Y indicates that a feature is supported. N indicates that a feature is not supported.

| Feature | ECS environment | Kubernetes environment | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deploy an application | Y | Y | The Kubernetes environment supports more instance scheduling policies and lets you deploy multiple instances on a single node. |
| Start an application | Y | Y | N/A |
| Stop an application | Y | Y | N/A |
| Delete an application | Y | Y | N/A |
| Scale an application | Y | Y | N/A |
| Reset an application | Y | N | This feature is not required in the Kubernetes environment. To reset an application, delete its pod. |
| Upgrade or downgrade a container | Y | Y | N/A |
| Roll back an application | Y | Y | N/A |
| Horizontal scaling | Y | Y | The methods and rules are different for each environment. |
| Scheduled scaling | N | Y | N/A |
| Batch deployment | Y | Y | N/A |
| Application groups | Y | N | N/A |
| Configuration of application groups | Y | N | N/A |

| Real-time logs | Y | Y | N/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log directory | Y | Y | N/A |
| SLS logs | Y | Y | N/A |
| Load balancing | Y | Y | N/A |
| Health check | Y | Y | The Kubernetes environment uses readiness and liveness probes, which are different from the health check mechanism in the ECS environment. |
| Java Virtual Machine (JVM) parameter configuration | Y | Y | N/A |
| Tomcat configuration | Y | Y | N/A |
| Lifecycle hooks | Y | Y | The Kubernetes environment supports PostStart and PreStop hooks, which are different from those in the ECS environment. |
| Environment variables | Y | Y | N/A |
| Canary release (phased release) | Y | Y | N/A |
| Traffic monitoring | Y | Y | N/A |
| Throttling and degradation | Y | Y | The Kubernetes environment allows for non-intrusive implementation. |
| Service list query | Y | Y | N/A |
| Configuration push | Y | Y | N/A |

| Event center | Y | Y | N/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notifications and alerts | Y | Y | N/A |
| Application diagnostics | Y | Y | Kubernetes supports more advanced, integrated diagnostics capabilities for monitoring and control. |
| Resource purchasing | Y | N | N/A |
| Service mesh | N | Y | N/A |
| Image-based deployment | N | Y | N/A |
| Multi-language support | N | Y | N/A |
| NAS support | N | Y | N/A |

**FAQ**

**Can I deploy multiple application instances on a single node in**

**the ECS environment?**

No, you cannot. If you have this requirement, use the Kubernetes environment.

**Can I deploy multi-language applications in the ECS**

**environment?**

No, you cannot. If you have this requirement, use the Kubernetes environment.

**Are the OpenAPI operations for the ECS and Kubernetes**

**environments the same?**

No, they are not. For a list of the OpenAPI operations for the ECS and Kubernetes environments, see the **EDAS Developer Guide > Introduction to POP API Usage** .

**Do both the ECS and Kubernetes environments support**

**developer tools?**

All are supported, but each has a different configuration.

**Do both the ECS and Kubernetes environments support Apsara**

**DevOps?**

Yes, they do. However, older versions of Apsara DevOps support deployment only in the ECS environment. Apsara DevOps 2020 supports deployment in both ECS and Kubernetes environments.

**How are node resources purchased and scaled out in the**

**Kubernetes environment?**

In the Kubernetes environment, elastic scaling refers to the scaling of pods. Typically, a Kubernetes cluster does not purchase new ECS instances (nodes) or release existing ones. You can use the features of Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) to implement elastic scaling for nodes.

**How do I migrate applications that use mounted scripts from**

**an ECS environment to a Kubernetes environment?**

In the ECS environment, mounted scripts run specified commands when the deployment process reaches a specific stage. You can mount scripts to four lifecycle stages: preparing an instance, starting the application, stopping the application, and destroying the instance. The Kubernetes environment provides only the PostStart and PreStop lifecycle hooks. These hooks do not directly correspond to the lifecycle stages of an ECS application. Therefore, you must modify your scripts when you migrate an application that uses mounted scripts to a Kubernetes environment. For scripts mounted to run before the instance preparation stage, orchestrate them into a Dockerfile and build them into the image. For scripts mounted to run before the application start stage, you can also orchestrate them into a Dockerfile and build them into the image. In a pod, preparing an instance and starting the application are part of the same process. For scripts mounted to run after the application start stage, configure them in the PostStart hook. For scripts mounted to run before the instance stop stage, configure them in the PreStop hook. For scripts mounted to run after the instance stops, perform cleanup during the application's graceful shutdown. For example, you can run cleanup tasks in a Java ShutdownHook or in a process that listens for the SIGTERM signal. You can also move the scripts to the PreStop hook if needed. For scripts mounted to run before the instance is destroyed, perform cleanup during the application's graceful shutdown. For example, you can run cleanup tasks in a Java ShutdownHook or in a process that listens for the SIGTERM signal. You can also move the scripts to the PreStop hook if needed. In a pod, destroying an instance and stopping an instance are part of the same process.

### Use a JAR or WAR package to

**deploy a Java microservices**

**application in an ACK cluster**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) fully integrates with Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) based on cloud-native Kubernetes. EDAS allows you to manage the full lifecycle of Kubernetes containerized applications. An ACK cluster is embedded with the capabilities of Alibaba Cloud in virtual machines, storage, networking, and security, and provides an excellent runtime environment for Kubernetes containerized applications. This topic describes how to use a JAR or WAR package provided by EDAS to deploy a Java application in an ACK cluster.

**Background information**

To deploy an application in an ACK cluster, create an ACK cluster in the ACK console first. Then, import the cluster to EDAS, and use a deployment package to deploy the application in the imported cluster.

| Create an ACK cluster |   | Import the ACK cluster to EDAS |   | Deploy an application in the ACK cluster |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**Note**

JAR or WAR packages can be used to create only Java applications. For more information about how to use an image to deploy a Java application or an application of different programming languages, see Use an image to deploy an application in an ACK cluster or Deploy multi-language microservices to K8s with images.

**Prerequisites**

EDAS and ACK are activated for your Apsara Stack tenant account.

**Step 1: Create an ACK cluster**

1. Log in to the ACK console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. On the Clusters page, click **Create**
**Kubernetes Cluster** in the upper-right corner of the page.
3. On the **ACK Dedicated** tab of the **Create Kubernetes Cluster** page, configure the basic
settings of the cluster.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Cluster Name | The name of the cluster. The name must be 1 to 63 characters in length and can contain digits, letters, and hyphens (-). Note The cluster name must be unique among clusters that belong to the same Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| Resource Set | The resource set to which the cluster belongs. A resource set is a container used to store resources. Each resource must belong to a resource set. After you select a resource set, virtual private clouds (VPCs) and vSwitches are filtered based on the selected resource set. |
| Region | The region in which you want to deploy the cluster. |

| IPv4/IPv6 Dual- stack | Specifies whether to enable IPv4/IPv6 dual stack. Note You can enable IPv4/IPv6 dual stack only for clusters that run Kubernetes 1.20 or later. Master nodes and worker nodes still use IPv4 addresses to communicate with each other in a cluster. You must select Terway as the network plug-in. You must use a VPC and Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances that support IPv4/IPv6 dual stack. |
|---|---|
| VPC | The VPC in which you want to deploy the cluster. |
| vSwitch | The vSwitches that you want to use. You can select up to three vSwitches that are deployed in differentz ones. |
| Kubernetes Version | The Kubernetes version of the cluster. |
| Container Runtime | Only containerd is supported. You must deploy ECS bare metal instances. We recommend that you select the latest version available in the ACK console. |
| Master Nodes | The number of master nodes that you want to use. You can create three or five master nodes. Note You can create a single master node. By default, this feature is unavailable. To use this feature, contact the technical support of Apsara Stack. |
| Instance Type | The instance type of master nodes. You can select multiple instance types. You can also select a dedicated host group for the master nodes. For more information, see Instance types in the ECS documentation. |

| System Disk | The system disk category. Valid values: Ultra Disk, Premium Performance Disk, SSD Disk, and Standard Performance Disk. Note You can select Encrypt Disk to encrypt disks. To encrypt disks, you need to configure the following parameters: Encryption method: You can select AES256 or SM4. Encryption key: You can select a key that is created in Key Management Service (KMS). Encryption is supported only when you select Premium Performance Disk or Standard Performance Disk as the system disk category. |
|---|---|

| Mount Data Disk | The data disk category. Valid values: Ultra Disk, Premium Performance Disk, SSD Disk, and Standard Performance Disk. Note You can select Encrypt Disk to encrypt data disks. To encrypt data disks, you need to configure the following parameters: Encryption method: You can select AES256 or SM4. Encryption key: You can select a key that is created in Key Management Service (KMS). For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes of a version earlier than 1.32, ACK automatically formats the last data disk if you add two or more data disks, mounts the data disk to /var/lib/container , and mounts /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.32 or later, you can customize the data disk formatting setting. You can choose one of the following data disk formatting options: Not Formatted: does not format the data disk and retains the original data in the disk. Format and use as container runtime directory: formats the data disk and uses it as the container runtime directory. Format and configure custom mount directory: formats the data disk and mounts it to the user-defined path. For more information, see the How do I specify a mount directory for data disks in a node pool? section of this topic. Important If two or more disks are formatted, you must specify only one disk as the container runtime directory. Each node must have a disk used as the container runtime directory. If no disk is specified, ACK automatically uses the last data disk. In this case, ACK will automatically format the disk, mount the disk to /var/lib/container , and mount /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . |
|---|---|
| Deployment Set | You must first create a deployment set in the ECS console and select the deployment set for control plane nodes in the ACK console. Important You cannot change the deployment set used by control planes after the control planes are created. |
| Worker Instance | By default, Create Instance is selected. |

|   | /var/lib/container |   |
|---|---|---|
| /var/lib/kubelet |   |   |

| Sandbox | Specifies whether to enable Sandboxed-Container. Agent Sandbox is a production-grade sandbox runtime for AI agents. It provides isolated execution environments for untrusted applications. It applies only to ECS instance nodes. Note After Sandboxed-Container is enabled: You cannot select Dedicated Host Groups. The system automatically deploys the runSC runtime and related components. The system provides only the ECS instance types (Intel/Hygon) supported by sandboxes. Operating System: You can select only Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 series that use MLPS-compliant images. |
|---|---|
| Dedicated Host Groups | You can select a dedicated host group for worker nodes. Note This parameter is not displayed after you select Enable Sandbox. |
| Instance Type | The instance type of worker nodes. You can select one or more instance types. For more information, see Instance types in the ECS documentation. |
| Selected Types | The selected instance types. |
| Quantity | The number of worker nodes. |
| System Disk | The system disk category. Valid values: Ultra Disk, Premium Performance Disk, SSD Disk, and Standard Performance Disk. Note You can select Encrypt Disk to encrypt disks. Encryption is supported only when you select Premium Performance Disk or Standard Performance Disk as the system disk category. |

| Mount Data Disk | The data disk category. Valid values: Ultra Disk, Premium Performance Disk, SSD Disk, and Standard Performance Disk. You can select Encrypt Disk to encrypt disks. For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes of a version earlier than 1.32, ACK automatically formats the last data disk if you add two or more data disks, mounts the data disk to /var/lib/container , and mounts /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.32 or later, you can customize the data disk formatting setting. You can choose one of the following data disk formatting options: Not Formatted: does not format the data disk and retains the original data in the disk. Format and use as container runtime directory: formats the data disk and uses it as the container runtime directory. Format and configure custom mount directory: formats the data disk and mounts it to the user-defined path. For more information, see the How do I specify a mount directory for data disks in a node pool? section of this topic. Important If two or more disks are formatted, you must specify only one disk as the container runtime directory. Each node must have a disk used as the container runtime directory. If no disk is specified, ACK automatically uses the last data disk. In this case, ACK will automatically format the disk, mount the disk to /var/lib/container , and mount /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . Note You cannot specify an encryption algorithm for data disks. |
|---|---|

|   | /var/lib/container |   |
|---|---|---|
| /var/lib/kubelet |   |   |

| Network Plug- in | The network plug-in of the cluster. Valid values: Flannel and Terway. By default, Flannel is selected. If you select Flannel, you must also specify the Number of Pods per Node, Flannel Mode, Pod CIDR Block, and Service CIDR parameters. Number of Pods per Node: Specify the maximum number of pods on a node. Flannel Mode: If you select Enable Flannel VXLAN mode, you can enable cross-node container network communication through Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) tunnels. Pod CIDR Block: Specify the CIDR block of pods. The pod CIDR block cannot overlap with the CIDR block of the VPC that you select or the CIDR blocks of existing ACK clusters in the VPC that you select. The pod CIDR block cannot be modified after the cluster is created. The Service CIDR block cannot overlap with the pod CIDR block. Service CIDR: Specify the CIDR block of Services. The Service CIDR block cannot overlap with the CIDR block of the VPC that you select or the CIDR blocks of existing ACK clusters in the VPC that you select. The Service CIDR block cannot overlap with the pod CIDR block. The Service CIDR block cannot be modified after the cluster is created. If you select Terway, the DataPath V2, Support for NetworkPolicy, and Support for ENI Trunking options are available. Pod vSwitch: You need to specify at least one pod vSwitch for each node vSwitch in the same zone. Service CIDR: Specify the CIDR block of Services. The Service CIDR block cannot overlap with the CIDR block of the VPC that you select or the CIDR blocks of existing ACK clusters in the VPC that you select. The Service CIDR block cannot overlap with the pod CIDR block. The Service CIDR block cannot be modified after the cluster is created. IPv6 Service CIDR: After IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack is enabled, you need to specify an IPv6 CIDR block for Services. When you set this parameter, take note of the following items: You must specify a unique local address (ULA) space within the address range fc00::/7. The prefix must be 112 bits to 120 bits in length. We recommend that you specify an IPv6 CIDR block that has the same number of IP addresses as the Service CIDR block. For more information, see Network planning in VPC User Guide. Note If you select a shared VPC for the cluster, only the Terway network plug- in is supported. |
|---|---|
| Operating System | You can select operating systems such as Alibaba Cloud Linux 3, Anolis OS, UOS, Kylin V10, Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 64-bit (MLPS 2.0 Level 3), and Alibaba Cloud Linux 4. |

| Security Hardening | Disable: disables MLPS Security Hardening for ECS instances. MLPS Security Hardening: enables MLPS Security Hardening for ECS instances. You can enable MLPS Security Hardening only when you select an Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 image. Alibaba Cloud provides baselines and the baseline check feature to help you check the compliance of Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 images with the level 3 standards of MLPS 2.0. For more information, see MLPS Security Hardening. Important MLPS Security Hardening enhances the security of OS images to meet the requirements of GB/T 22239-2019 Information Security Technology - Baseline for Classified Protection of Cybersecurity without compromising the compatibility and performance of the OS images. After you enable MLPS Security Hardening, root users cannot log in over SSH. You can use Virtual Network Computing (VNC) to log in to the operating system from the ECS console and create regular users who are allowed to log in over SSH. |
|---|---|
| Logon Type | Key Pair Key Pair: Select a key pair from the drop-down list. If you do not have key pairs, create one in the ECS console. Password Password: Enter the password that is used to log in to the nodes. Confirm Password: Enter the password again to confirm it. Note The password must be 8 to 30 characters in length and must contain at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. The password cannot contain underscores ( ). _ |

| Configure SNAT | Specifies whether to enable Configure SNAT for VPC. If you select Configure SNAT for VPC, a NAT gateway is configured for the selected VPC. If a NAT gateway already exists in the selected VPC: No VPC-specific SNAT entries are created: The system automatically creates vSwitch-specific SNAT entries for all vSwitches used by the ACK cluster. VPC-specific SNAT entries exist: No operation is performed. If the selected VPC does not have a NAT gateway, a NAT gateway is automatically created and vSwitch-specific SNAT entries are configured for all vSwitches used by the ACK cluster. Note If you disallow the system to automatically create a NAT gateway and want the VPC to access the Internet, you must manually associate the VPC with a NAT gateway or create SNAT entries for the VPC. |
|---|---|
| API Server Access | By default, an internal-facing Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance is created for the API server. You can change the type of the SLB instance. If you delete the SLB instance, the API server becomes inaccessible. Specify whether to enable Expose API Server with EIP: The API server provides multiple HTTP-based RESTful APIs that can be used to create, delete, modify, query, and watch resource objects such as pods and Services. If you select the check box, an elastic IP address (EIP) is created and attached to an internal-facing SLB instance. In this case, port 6443 used by the API server is exposed on master nodes. You can use a kubeconfig file to connect to the cluster over the Internet and manage the cluster. If you clear the check box, no EIP is created. You can use a kubeconfig file to connect to the cluster only from within the VPC and manage the cluster. |
| SSH Logon | To enable SSH login, you must select Expose API Server with EIP. If you enable SSH login over the Internet, you can access the cluster by using SSH. If you disable SSH login over the Internet, you cannot access the cluster by using SSH or kubectl. If you want to access an ECS instance in the cluster by using SSH, you must bind an EIP to the ECS instance and configure security group rules to open SSH port 22. |
| Security Group | The security group of the cluster. You can select Create Basic Security Group, Create Advanced Security Group, or Select Existing Security Group. For more information about security groups, see Create a security group in ECS User Guide. |

| Ingress | Select or clear Install Ingress Controllers. By default, Install Ingress Controllers is selected. After you select the check box, you can select APIG Ingress, Higress Ingress, or Nginx Ingress. NGINX Ingress is no longer available after Apsara Stack V3.18.6 2605 is released. Note We recommend that you install an Ingress controller if you want to expose Services. APIG Ingress: This option is displayed only when API Gateway is deployed in the current cloud. After you install the APIGateway Ingress component, the system automatically creates an API gateway that has 2 cores and 4 GB of memory and grants the required permissions to API Gateway. Note APIG Ingress provides fully managed services, high-availability SLA guarantees, and professional technical support, making it the optimal choice for production environments. Before you install API Gateway Ingress Controller, you must complete the RAM role authorization for API Gateway. If you have not yet completed this step, click Authorize to proceed with the authorization before installation. SLB Network Type: You can select Public Network or Private Network. Higress Ingress: If you select Higress Ingress, you must also configure SLB Network Type and SLB Specifications. Nginx Ingress: If you select Nginx Ingress, you must also configure the following parameters: SLB Source: You can select Create SLB Instance or Use Existing SLB Instance. If you select Use Existing SLB Instance, you need to select an SLB instance from the drop-down list. If you select Create SLB Instance, you need to specify SLB Network Type and SLB Specifications. SLB Network Type: You can select Public Network or Private Network. The LoadBalancer Service differs from the Internet-facing SLB instance associated with the preceding API Gateway Ingress. SLB Specifications: Select an SLB instance type. |
|---|---|
| Log Service | Specifies whether to enable Simple Log Service (SLS). If you enable SLS, you can select an existing project or create a project. If you select Enable Log Service, the SLS plug-in is automatically installed in the cluster. If you select Create Ingress Dashboard, Ingress access logs are collected and displayed on dashboards. If you select Install node-problem-detector and Create Event Center, Event Center is enabled to provide capabilities such as event storage, event retrieval, and event-driven alerting. By default, Event Center retains events for 90 days free of charge. |

| Monitoring Agent | Specifies whether to enable Managed Service for Prometheus. Select or clear Enable Prometheus Monitoring. Managed Service for Prometheus provides the basic monitoring and alerting features for the cluster. Note By default, the number of Prometheus replicas is 1. You can find the ack- arms-prometheus component on the Add-ons page and click Configuration to update the number of Prometheus replicas. The update takes effect immediately. |
|---|---|
| Alerts | If you select Use Default Alert Template, default alert rules are created. After the cluster is created, you can go to the details page of the cluster and choose Operations > Alerts to manage alert rules. For more information, see Alert configurations. Note To enable the alert management feature, you must create an event center in SLS and activate Managed Service for Prometheus for your cluster. |
| Volume Plug-in | By default, CSI is selected. |
| RRSA OIDC | You can enable the RAM Roles for Service Accounts (RRSA) feature for the cluster to enforce access control on different pods that are deployed in an ACK cluster. This implements fine-grained API permission control on pods. |
| AI Suite | Select the AI suite to be deployed with the cluster. The following suites are supported: Deploy training and inference components: deploys the ack-arena, kea, cert-manager, and ack-kserve components with the default parameter configurations. Deploy Task Scheduling Components: deploys the kube-queue component to implement task scheduling. Enable Data Acceleration: deploys the fluid component to accelerate access to Object Storage Service (OSS). Enable Image Acceleration: deploys the aliyun-acr-acceleration-suite and ack-dragonfly components to implement image acceleration. |
| Cluster Deletion Protection | Specifies whether to enable the deletion protection feature for the cluster. If you select the check box, the cluster cannot be deleted in the ACK console or by calling API operations. |
| Node Protection | Specifies whether to enable node protection. The check box is selected by default to prevent nodes from being deleted in the ACK console or by calling API operations. |
| Labels | Add labels to nodes in the cluster. |

4. Click **Show Advanced Options** at the bottom of the page to configure advanced settings
for the cluster.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Custom Image | The custom image to be used. After you select a custom image, all nodes in the cluster are deployed by using this image. |
| Kube-proxy Mode | The kube-proxy mode in which cluster Services distribute requests to backend pods. Valid values: iptables and IPVS. iptables: a mature and stable kube-proxy mode. It uses iptables rules to perform Service discovery and load balancing. The performance of this mode is limited by the size of the cluster. This mode is suitable for clusters that run a small number of Services. IPVS: a high-performance kube-proxy mode. It uses Linux IP Virtual Server (IPVS) to perform Service discovery and load balancing. This mode is suitable for clusters that run a large number of Services. We recommend that you use this mode in scenarios where high-performance load balancing is required. |
| Node Port Range | The node port range. |
| Taints | Add taints to all worker nodes in the cluster. |
| Cluster Domain Name | The default domain name is cluster.local. You can enter a custom domain name. |
| Custom Node Name | Specify whether to use a custom node name. A custom node name consists of a prefix, an IP substring, and a suffix. The prefix and suffix can contain multiple parts that are separated by periods (.). Each part can contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-), and must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit. The IP substring length specifies the number of digits to be truncated from the end of the node IP address. The IP substring length ranges from 5 to 12. For example, if the node IP address is 192.1XX.X.XX, the prefix is aliyun.com, the IP substring length is 5, and the suffix is test, the node name will be aliyun.com00055test. |
| Cluster CA | Specifies whether to enable the cluster certification authority (CA) certificate. |
| User Data | Customize the startup behaviors of the ECS instances and import data to the ECS instances. The user data can be used to perform the following operations: Run scripts during instance startup. Pass user data as common data into an ECS instance for future reference. |

5. On the right side of the page, click **Create Cluster**.
6. In the **Confirm** dialog box, make sure that all check items are verified, read and select the
Terms of Service and disclaimer, and then click **OK** to start the deployment. After the cluster is created, you can view the cluster on the **Clusters** page.

**Step 2: Import the ACK cluster to EDAS in the EDAS console**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resource Management > Container Service**
**Kubernetes Clusters**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select the region in which you want to import the cluster, and
click **Synchronize Container Service Kubernetes Cluster**.
4. In the **Actions** column of the ACK cluster that you want to import, click **Import**.
5. In the **Precheck for Import** dialog box, click **Continue**.
6. In the **Import Kubernetes Cluster** dialog box, select the microservices namespace to
which you want to import the ACK cluster from the **Microservice Namespace** drop-down list, and click **Import**. If the value of the Cluster Status parameter is **Running** and the value of the **Import**
**Status** parameter is **Imported** for the ACK cluster, the ACK cluster is imported to EDAS.

**Step 3: Deploy an application in the ACK cluster**

**Note**

The procedure of deploying an application by using a WAR package is the same as that by using a JAR package. The example in this topic shows you how to use a JAR package to deploy an application.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**. In
the top navigation bar, select a region. In the upper part of the Applications page, select a microservices namespace from the **Microservice Namespace** drop-down list. Then, click
**Create Application** in the upper-left corner of the **Applications** page.
3. In the **Application Information** step, configure the parameters in the **Cluster Type** and
**Application Runtime Environment** sections, and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Cluster Type | Select Kubernetes Cluster. Note ACK clusters can be integrated with Apsara Stack Service Mesh (ASM). |
| Application Runtime Environment |   |
| Hosted Applications | The programming language based on which the application is developed. This topic describes how to deploy a Java application. In this example, Java is selected. For more information about how to deploy an application of different programming languages, see Deploy multi-language microservices to K8s with images. |
| Select Application | The runtime environment of the application. This topic describes how to use a JAR or WAR package to deploy a Java application. Select Java, Tomcat, EDAS-Container (HSF). or Alibaba application server based on the type of your application and deployment package. Java: Select this option if you want to use a universal JAR package to deploy the application as a Dubbo or a Spring Boot application. You can set the Java Environment parameter after you select this option. Tomcat: Select this option if you want to use a universal WAR package to deploy a Dubbo or a Spring application. You can set the Java Environment and Container Version parameters after you select this option. EDAS-Container (HSF): Select this option if you want to use a WAR or FatJar package to deploy the application as a High-speed Service Framework (HSF) application. You can set the Java Environment, Pandora Version, and Ali-Tomcat Version parameters after you select this option. Alibaba application server: This environment is suitable for deploying Java 2 Platform, Enterprise Edition (J2EE) applications and supports WAR, JAR (EJB), Enterprise Application Archive (EAR), and ZIP applications. You can set the Java Environment and Alibaba application server version parameters after you select this option. |
| Monitoring and Governance Solution | The microservices monitoring and governance solution. By default, a Java agent is mounted to the application runtime environment for an ACK cluster to implement fine-grained monitoring. In addition, EDAS provides complete solutions for microservices governance, such as canary releases, service authentication, throttling, and degradation. |

4. In the **Application Configuration** step, configure the environment information, basic
information, deployment method, and resource parameters for the application, and then click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Microservice Namespace | The microservices namespace in which you want to deploy the application. Select the microservices namespace that you created. If you do not have or select a microservices namespace, this parameter is set to Default. If you have not created a microservices namespace or you want to create a microservices namespace, click Create Microservice Namespace. For more information, see Manage microservices namespaces in the EDAS console. |
| Cluster | The cluster in which you want to deploy the application. Select the imported ACK cluster from the Cluster drop-down list. If the selected ACK cluster is not imported to EDAS, select This cluster is used for the first time in EDAS. If you select this check box, the cluster is imported to EDAS when an application is created. This consumes a certain amount of time. Then, specify whether to activate ASM. Note You can select a cluster that does not reside in the same microservices namespace as the application. |

| K8s Namespace | The Kubernetes namespace of the application. Internal system objects are allocated to different Kubernetes namespaces to form logically isolated projects, teams, or user groups. This way, different groups can be separately managed and share the resources of the entire cluster. Valid values: default: the default Kubernetes namespace. If an object does not belong to a Kubernetes namespace, the default Kubernetes namespace is used for the object. kube-system: the Kubernetes namespace for the objects that are created by the system. kube-public: the Kubernetes namespace that is automatically created by the system. This Kubernetes namespace can be read by all users, including unauthenticated users. In this example, default is selected. If you want to create a custom Kubernetes namespace, click Create Kubernetes Namespace. In the dialog box that appears, enter a name for the Kubernetes namespace in the K8s Namespace field. The name can contain digits, lowercase letters, and hyphens (-), and can be 1 to 63 characters in length. It must start and end with a letter or a digit. |
|---|---|
| Application Name | The name of the application. The name can contain digits, letters, and hyphens (-). It must start with a letter. The name can be up to 36 characters in length. |
| Application Alias | The application alias. |
| Application Description | The description of the application. The description can be up to 128 characters in length. |
| Image Type | The type of your container image. |
| Mirror pull strategy | Select an image pulling policy based on your business requirements. Always: Forcibly pull the latest image from the remote image repository each time the container is started. IfNotPresent: Pull the image from the remote image repository only when the image does not exist on the local computer. Never: Only local images are used. No image is pulled from the remote image repository. |

| Source of Deployment Package | Custom Program If you select this option, you must specify the File Uploading Method parameter. Valid values: Upload Jar Package: Select and upload the JAR package that you downloaded. JAR Package Address: Enter the address of your demo package. Official Demo EDAS provides the following types of demos: Spring Cloud Server Application, Spring Cloud Client Application, Dubbo Server Application, and Dubbo Client Application. Select a demo type based on your business requirements. |
|---|---|
| Version | The version number of your application. Specify a custom version number or click Use Timestamp as Version Number to generate a version number. |
| Time Zone | The time zone of the application. |
| Total Pods | The number of pods on which you want to deploy an application. |
| Single Pod Resource Quota | The amount of CPU and memory resources that you want to reserve for a pod. To set a limit, enter a numeric value. The default value 0 indicates that no limit is set on the CPU and memory quotas. Note For more information about how to configure ACK resource quotas, see Container Service for Kubernetes User Guide > Configure resource quotas and limits. On the Resource Quotas tab, if you have specified CPU Limit, make sure that the value of CPU CPU Limit is not 0. On the Resource Quotas tab, if you have specified Memory Limit, make sure that the value of Memory CPU Limit is not 0. |

5. (Optional) Configure advanced parameters.
For more information, see Advanced settings.
6. Click **Create Application**.
It may take several minutes to deploy the application. During the process, you can view the change records to track the deployment progress of the application. For more information, see Application overview. After the application is deployed, you can view the pod status on the **Application Overview** page. If the pod is in the **Running** state, the application is published. You can click the state of the pod to view the advanced settings of the application instance, such as **Deployment**, **Pod**, and **Startup Command**.

**What to do next**

After the application is deployed, you can add an Internet-facing Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance to allow access to the application over the Internet. You can also add an internalfacing SLB instance to allow all nodes in the same VPC to access the application over an internal network. For more information, see Add Server Load Balancer (SLB) or Reuse a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance.

### Use an image to deploy a Java

**microservices application in an**

**ACK cluster**

EDAS, built on cloud native K8s, integrates ACK to provide full lifecycle management for containerized applications. ACK integrates Alibaba Cloud capabilities such as virtual machines, storage, network, and security to provide a cloud runtime environment for K8s containerized applications. This topic explains how to deploy a Java microservices application to a K8s cluster using an image.

**Background**

To deploy an application to a K8s cluster, create a K8s cluster in the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console, import it into EDAS, and then deploy the application to the cluster by using a deployment package.

**Note**

JAR and WAR packages support only Java applications. To deploy Java or multi-language applications by using an image, see Deploy multi-language microservice applications in a K8s environment by using an image.

**Prerequisites**

You have access to both EDAS and Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK). You have built an application image and pushed it to an image repository. For detailed steps, see Build an application image and Push a local image.

**Step 1: Create an ACK cluster**

1. Log in to the ACK console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. On the Clusters page, click **Create**
**Kubernetes Cluster** in the upper-right corner of the page.
3. On the **ACK Dedicated** tab of the **Create Kubernetes Cluster** page, configure the basic
settings of the cluster.

Master nodes and worker nodes still use IPv4 addresses to communicate with each other in a cluster. You must select Terway as the network plug-in. You must use a VPC and Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances that support IPv4/IPv6 dual stack. |

| vSwitch | The vSwitches that you want to use. You can select up to three vSwitches that are deployed in differentz ones. |

For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes of a version earlier than 1.32, ACK automatically formats the last data disk if you add two or more data disks, mounts the data disk to /var/lib/container , and mounts /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.32 or later, you can customize the data disk formatting setting. You can choose one of the following data disk formatting options: Not Formatted: does not format the data disk and retains the original data in the disk. Format and use as container runtime directory: formats the data disk and uses it as the container runtime directory. Format and configure custom mount directory: formats the data disk and mounts it to the user-defined path. For more information, see the How do I specify a mount directory for data disks in a node pool? section of this topic. Important If two or more disks are formatted, you must specify only one disk as the container runtime directory. Each node must have a disk used as the container runtime directory. If no disk is specified, ACK automatically uses the last data disk. In this case, ACK will automatically format the disk, mount the disk to /var/lib/container , and mount /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . |
|---|---|
| Deployment Set | You must first create a deployment set in the ECS console and select the deployment set for control plane nodes in the ACK console. Important You cannot change the deployment set used by control planes after the control planes are created. |

|   | /var/lib/container |   |
|---|---|---|
| /var/lib/kubelet |   |   |

| Worker Instance | By default, Create Instance is selected. |
|---|---|
| Sandbox | Specifies whether to enable Sandboxed-Container. Agent Sandbox is a production-grade sandbox runtime for AI agents. It provides isolated execution environments for untrusted applications. It applies only to ECS instance nodes. Note After Sandboxed-Container is enabled: You cannot select Dedicated Host Groups. The system automatically deploys the runSC runtime and related components. The system provides only the ECS instance types (Intel/Hygon) supported by sandboxes. Operating System: You can select only Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 series that use MLPS-compliant images. |

Encryption is supported only when you select Premium Performance Disk or Standard Performance Disk as the system disk category. |

For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes of a version earlier than 1.32, ACK automatically formats the last data disk if you add two or more data disks, mounts the data disk to /var/lib/container , and mounts /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . For ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.32 or later, you can customize the data disk formatting setting. You can choose one of the following data disk formatting options: Not Formatted: does not format the data disk and retains the original data in the disk. Format and use as container runtime directory: formats the data disk and uses it as the container runtime directory. Format and configure custom mount directory: formats the data disk and mounts it to the user-defined path. For more information, see the How do I specify a mount directory for data disks in a node pool? section of this topic. Important If two or more disks are formatted, you must specify only one disk as the container runtime directory. Each node must have a disk used as the container runtime directory. If no disk is specified, ACK automatically uses the last data disk. In this case, ACK will automatically format the disk, mount the disk to /var/lib/container , and mount /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . Note You cannot specify an encryption algorithm for data disks. |

**Step 2: Import the ACK cluster to EDAS in the EDAS console**

**Always**: Forcibly pull the latest image from the remote image repository each time the

If the pod is in the **Running** state, the application is published. **What to do next**

After the application is deployed, you can add an Internet-facing Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance to allow access to the application over the Internet. You can also add an internalfacing SLB instance to allow all nodes in the same VPC to access the application over an internal network. For more information, see Add Server Load Balancer (SLB) or Reuse a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance.

### Deploy Java microservice

**applications in an ECS**

**environment**

To help you quickly learn how to deploy microservice applications in Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS), EDAS provides microservice application demos for Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and High-speed Service Framework (HSF). You can deploy the application demos to a specified ECS cluster. This topic describes how to deploy a microservice application in an ECS environment using an example.

**Prerequisites**

Import ECS Create an ECS cluster

**Background information**

The EDAS console provides a pair of microservice application demos for each of the Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and HSF frameworks. You can use these demos to perform simple service invocations. The deployment procedures for application demos that use different frameworks are nearly identical. This topic uses a Spring Cloud application demo as an example. For more information about the demos, see alibabacloud-microservice-demo. If you want to learn how to implement the features of a microservice application, see Application development overview.

**Deploy an application demo**

The microservice application demo contains a server application (service provider) and a client application (service consumer). This topic describes how to deploy the server application. After you deploy the server application, you can follow the same procedure to deploy the client application.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**. In
the top navigation bar, select a region. In the upper part of the Applications page, select a microservices namespace from the **Microservice Namespace** drop-down list. Then, click
**Create Application** in the upper-left corner of the **Applications** page.
3. On the **Create Application** page, on the **Basic Information** tab, set the application's
basic information and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |

Note This topic uses the deployment of a Spring Cloud application JAR package demo as an example. Therefore, Java is selected for Application Runtime Environment. To deploy a WAR package for a Spring Cloud or Dubbo application, or an HSF application, select the appropriate application runtime environment and version as prompted on the interface. |
|---|---|
| Application Name | Enter an application name. |
| Application Alias | Enter an application alias. |
| Application Description | Enter a description for the application. The description can be up to 128 characters in length. |

4. On the **Configurations** tab, configure the deployment package and environment for the
application, and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |

| Instance Source | The default value is Use Existing Instance. This parameter cannot be changed. |

| Microservices Namespace | Select the microservices namespace where the cluster is created. You can also click +Create Microservices Namespace to the right of the drop-down list to create a microservices namespace. Note If the cluster is created in the default microservices namespace, select the default microservices namespace. |
| Cluster | Select the created cluster. You can also click +Create Cluster to the right of the drop-down list to create a cluster. |

After the deployment begins, a message appears at the top of the **Basic Information** page: A deployment is in progress for the application. The deployment takes approximately 2 minutes. You can also click **View Details** next to the message to view the deployment progress and related logs on the application's **Change Details** page.

2. On the **Basic Information** page in the client application, click **Instance Deployment**
**Information**.
3. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, copy the public IP address of the ECS
instance that runs the client application.
4. Use a browser to access the URL of the client application. The format is `http://<Public IP`
`address of the ECS instance>:8080` . Verify that the web page of the client application is accessible. `Hello EDAS`, and click **Click Here**.

Verify that the string is echoed at the bottom of the page. ### Deploy multi-language

**microservices to K8s with images**

An increasing number of microservices applications use multiple programming languages such as Python, Go, and Node.js. Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) allows you to deploy multi-language microservices applications in Kubernetes clusters by using a service mesh. EDAS provides the following service governance capabilities for microservices applications: application management, service discovery, tracing analysis, load balancing, and application monitoring. This topic provides an example on how to use images to deploy multi-language microservices applications in Kubernetes clusters in EDAS.

**Prerequisites**

An application image is created and uploaded to your Apsara Stack image repository. For more information, see Create an application image and Upload an on-premises image. To experience the deployment practice, you can use the sample application provided by EDAS. You can download the application from Bookinfo Sample.

**Background information**

Applications have evolved from the original monolithic architecture to the current microservices architecture. The microservices architecture facilitates application development but increases complexity in service deployment and O&M. You can deploy applications that are developed in any programming languages as microservices. To provide service governance capabilities for these microservices, such as tracing analysis, service discovery, and load balancing, you can use either multi-language SDKs or service meshes. SDKs are intrusive to multi-language microservices applications. Service meshes can provide capabilities such as service discovery, load balancing, and tracing analysis while remaining non-intrusive to multi-language microservices applications. Therefore, EDAS offers the service mesh feature for multi-language microservices applications. A service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer that implements service-to-service communication. A service mesh provides a stable and reliable method to deliver requests. If you use a service mesh, you do not need to be concerned about the complex topology of services that compose a modern, cloud-native application. In most cases, a service mesh is implemented as an array of lightweight network proxies that are deployed in combination with an application code. This way, you do not need to be concerned about the status of the application.

**Sample scenario**

BookInfo is an application that displays the detailed information about a book. The application functions as a filter for an online bookstore. The application displays the description of a book, the book details such as the International Standard Book Number (ISBN) and the number of pages, and reviews on the book. BookInfo is a heterogeneous application that consists of several microservices applications. These microservices applications are developed in different programming languages. These microservices applications form a classic service mesh, which consists of multiple microservices that are written in different programming languages. Among these microservices, the Reviews microservice has multiple versions. Figure 1. Architecture for multi-language microservices The BookInfo application consists of the following four independent microservices: Productpage: a Python microservice that calls the Details and Reviews microservices to generate a page. The Productpage microservice provides the login and logout features. Details: a Ruby microservice that contains book information. Reviews: a Java microservice that provides book reviews and calls the Ratings microservice. The Reviews microservice has the following three versions: Version 1, which does not call the Ratings microservice. Version 2, which calls the Ratings microservice and rates a book by using one to five black stars. Version 3, which calls the Ratings microservice and rates a book by using one to five red stars. Ratings: a Node.js microservice that provides ratings generated based on book reviews.

**Procedure**

Before you can deploy a multi-language microservices application in a Kubernetes cluster, you must create a Kubernetes cluster in the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console and import the cluster to EDAS in the EDAS console. Then, you can use a custom image to deploy an application in the cluster.

**Step 1: Create an ACK cluster**

1. Log in to the ACK console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. On the Clusters page, click **Create**
**Kubernetes Cluster** in the upper-right corner of the page.
3. On the **ACK Dedicated** tab of the **Create Kubernetes Cluster** page, configure the basic
settings of the cluster.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Cluster Name | The name of the cluster. The name must be 1 to 63 characters in length and can contain digits, letters, and hyphens (-). Note The cluster name must be unique among clusters that belong to the same Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| Resource Set | The resource set to which the cluster belongs. A resource set is a container used to store resources. Each resource must belong to a resource set. After you select a resource set, virtual private clouds (VPCs) and vSwitches are filtered based on the selected resource set. |
| Region | The region in which you want to deploy the cluster. |

| IPv4/IPv6 Dual- stack | Specifies whether to enable IPv4/IPv6 dual stack. Note You can enable IPv4/IPv6 dual stack only for clusters that run Kubernetes 1.20 or later. Master nodes and worker nodes still use IPv4 addresses to communicate with each other in a cluster. You must select Terway as the network plug-in. You must use a VPC and Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances that support IPv4/IPv6 dual stack. |

If no disk is specified, ACK automatically uses the last data disk. In this case, ACK will automatically format the disk, mount the disk to /var/lib/container , and mount /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd to /var/lib/container . |

It uses iptables rules to perform Service discovery and load balancing. The performance of this mode is limited by the size of the cluster. This mode is suitable for clusters that run a small number of Services. IPVS: a high-performance kube-proxy mode. It uses Linux IP Virtual Server (IPVS) to perform Service discovery and load balancing. This mode is suitable for clusters that run a large number of Services. We recommend that you use this mode in scenarios where high-performance load balancing is required. |

The prefix and suffix can contain multiple parts that are separated by periods (.). Each part can contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-), and must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit. The IP substring length specifies the number of digits to be truncated from the end of the node IP address. The IP substring length ranges from 5 to 12. For example, if the node IP address is 192.1XX.X.XX, the prefix is aliyun.com, the IP substring length is 5, and the suffix is test, the node name will be aliyun.com00055test. |

**Step 2: Import the ACK cluster to EDAS in the EDAS console**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resource Management > Container Service**
**Kubernetes Clusters**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select the region in which you want to import the cluster, and
click **Synchronize Container Service Kubernetes Cluster**.
4. In the **Actions** column of the ACK cluster that you want to import, click **Import**.
5. In the **Precheck for Import** dialog box, click **Continue**.
6. In the **Import Kubernetes Cluster** dialog box, select the microservices namespace to
which you want to import the ACK cluster from the **Microservice Namespace** drop-down list, and click **Import**. If the value of the Cluster Status parameter is **Running** and the value of the **Import**
**Status** parameter is **Imported** for the ACK cluster, the ACK cluster is imported to EDAS.

**Deploy a multi-language microservices application in the**

**Kubernetes cluster**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**. In
the top navigation bar, select a region. In the upper part of the Applications page, select a microservices namespace from the Microservices Namespace drop-down list. Then, click

### FAQ for getting started

If you encounter problems when you create and deploy applications in EDAS, refer to the solutions in this topic.

**How to choose between an ECS cluster and a Kubernetes**

**cluster**

When you create an application, the first step is to select a cluster type. You can select a suitable cluster type based on the following criteria:

**Note**

If you are unsure which cluster type to select, select an ECS cluster.

| Cluster type | Deployment mode | O&M cost | Integration with cloud native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ECS cluster | One application is deployed on a single ECS instance. | The O&M is similar to traditional Linux operations. It has a low entry barrier and is easy to manage. | N/A |
| Kubernetes cluster | One application is deployed on a single pod. Multiple pods can run on a single ECS instance. | Requires a basic understanding of and experience with virtualization, container technology, and Kubernetes clusters. | Natively integrates with cloud native technologies. One image can run in multiple locations. |

**Why are only instance types available in a custom**

**environment?**

**Symptom**

On the **Application Configuration** page, only instance types are available for selection. VPCs and specific ECS instances are not displayed.

**Possible cause**

This issue occurs because no Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), microservices namespace, cluster, or Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance has been created for the current account in the current region. As a result, you only need to select an instance type. EDAS then creates a default VPC, an ECS instance of the specified type, a default microservices namespace, and a cluster for you.

**Solution**

If you have specific requirements for networking, service isolation, or ECS, first create the VPC, microservices namespace, cluster, and ECS instances. Then, you can select these resources on the page to deploy your application.

**Cluster import fails**

**Symptom**

On the **Application Configuration** page, select **Custom**. In the **Instance** section, select
**Use Existing Instances**, and then select **Instances Not Imported To A Cluster** . When
you create the application, an error message appears that indicates the instance failed to be imported into the cluster. For example: Failed to import the instance into the cluster. Only ECS instances that run 64-bit Aliyun Linux 2.1903 (Recommended) or 64-bit CentOS 6.9/7.2/7.3/7.4/7.6 can be imported into a cluster. Ensure that the operating system of the ECS instance that you want to import is supported.

**Possible cause**

The operating system of the selected ECS instance is not supported by EDAS.

**Solution**

Select another ECS instance. The operating system of the instance must be 64-bit Aliyun Linux 2.1903 or 64-bit CentOS 6.9/7.2/7.3/7.4/7.6.

**How to change the application port**

For applications deployed in an ECS cluster, you can change the application port by modifying the Tomcat port in the application configuration on the application details page. For applications deployed in a Kubernetes cluster, you can change the application port only by specifying it in the code or by attaching a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance. evelopment

## Application development

### Overview of application

**development**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) supports three microservices application frameworks: Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and High-speed Service Framework (HSF). You can use Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and HSF to develop applications and use EDAS to manage the applications.

| Application framework | Description | References |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Cloud | EDAS supports the native Spring Cloud microservice framework. You can deploy applications in EDAS to use its enterprise-level features, such as application management, microservice administration, monitoring and alerting, and application diagnostics, without the need to modify code or add configurations. The microservice administration features include service search, canary release, outlier ejection, and graceful shutdown. The features of EDAS help you make your applications more stable and secure. | Spring Cloud overview Implement service registration and discovery Implement load balancing Implement configuration management Build a service gateway |
| Dubbo | EDAS supports the Apache Dubbo microservice framework. You can deploy microservices developed with the Apache Dubbo framework to EDAS without changing your code. Simply add dependencies and modify configurations. After deployment, you gain access to enterprise-level EDAS features, such as microservice application hosting, microservice administration, monitoring and alerting, and application diagnostics. | Dubbo overview Use Spring Boot to develop a Dubbo microservice application |

evelopment

| HSF | HSF connects different business systems and decouples them by minimizing implementation dependencies. For distributed applications, HSF unifies the methods for publishing and calling services. This helps you develop distributed applications and use or provide common functional modules more easily and quickly. HSF abstracts away complex technical details of the distributed realm, such as remote communication, serialization, performance loss, and the implementation of synchronous and asynchronous calls. Note Dubbo 3.0 unifies the technologies of the Dubbo and HSF frameworks. In EDAS, you can easily upgrade HSF applications to Dubbo 3.0 applications. After the upgrade, HSF applications can continue to use their original development methods. They can also use the more comprehensive service administration features that EDAS provides for Dubbo applications. | HSF introduction Start the lightweight configuration and registration center Develop applications using Ali- Tomcat Develop applications using Pandora Boot A single call process Asynchronous calls Generalized calls Call context Serialization method selection Timeout configuration Server-side thread pool configuration API reference JVM -D startup configuration parameters |
