**ECS environment types**

EDAS supports Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters and hybrid cloud ECS clusters. Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster: A cluster that is created in a virtual private cloud (VPC) and consists of Alibaba Cloud ECS instances. For more information, see Create an ECS cluster using the console. Hybrid cloud ECS cluster: A cluster that is created in a VPC and contains Alibaba Cloud ECS instances and servers from an Internet Data Center (IDC) or other cloud service providers. For more information, see Create a Hybrid Cloud ECS Cluster.

**Application types supported in ECS environments**

You can use EDAS ECS environments to host applications that are developed using mainstream Java microservice frameworks, such as Spring Cloud and Dubbo. You can also host High-speed Service Framework (HSF) applications.

**Application hosting features provided by ECS environments**

ECS environments provide comprehensive capabilities for hosted applications, including application lifecycle management, service administration, monitoring, O&M, and resource management. anagement for ECS clusters

You can deploy applications from JAR or WAR packages. | For more information, see Application Creation and Deployment Overview (ECS). |

If an issue occurs in the new version after an upgrade, you can roll back the application to a previous version. | For more information, see Upgrade and rollback applications (ECS). |

### Resource management

#### Overview of ECS resource management

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) offering that provides application environments in Elastic Compute Service (ECS) and Kubernetes. This topic describes the resources in the ECS environment and how to manage them in EDAS. The ECS environment in EDAS includes microservices namespaces, virtual private clouds (VPCs), clusters, and ECS instances.

| Reso urce | Purpose | EDAS management operations | Documentation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Micro servic es name space | Microservices namespaces provide isolated runtime environments, such as development, test, and production. They allow you to isolate resources and services and manage them from a single account. | You can create, edit, and delete microservices namespaces. | For more information, see Manage microservices namespaces in the EDAS console. |

anagement for ECS clusters

| VPC | VPCs are private network services provided by Alibaba Cloud that are logically isolated from each other. If you have high network security requirements, you can create clusters and deploy applications in VPCs. | You can create and manage VPCs in the VPC console. Changes automatically sync to EDAS. | For more information, see Sync a VPC. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clust er | A cluster is a collection of cloud resources required to run applications. EDAS provides two types of ECS clusters: Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters and hybrid cloud ECS clusters. | You can create, scale out (add instances), manage, and delete Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters and hybrid cloud ECS clusters. Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters Create an ECS cluster in the console Scale out an ECS cluster in the console Manage ECS clusters Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster | Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters For more information, see Create an ECS cluster in the EDAS console. For more information, see Scale out an ECS cluster in the EDAS console. For more information, see Manage ECS clusters. Hybrid cloud ECS clusters For more information, see Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster. |
| ECS | ECS is a fundamental cloud computing service provided by Alibaba Cloud. You can use ECS instances to deploy applications. | EDAS provides a link to the ECS buy page where you can create instances. #### Microservice namespace management

##### Manage microservices namespaces in the

**console**

anagement for ECS clusters Microservices namespaces provide isolated runtime environments for applications, such as development, testing, and production environments. You can use microservices namespaces to isolate services. You cannot create two microservices namespaces with the same name in the same region.

**Scenarios**

For example, if you have three environments in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) for application development, testing, and production, you can create a separate microservices namespace for each environment, such as Dev, Test, and Prod. Applications and services in different microservices namespaces are isolated from each other. You cannot call services or push configurations across microservices namespaces.

**Default microservices namespace**

When you create an application in EDAS, you can select the **Default** microservices namespace. The default microservices namespace indicates that no microservices namespace is used. This means that the application does not use any microservices namespace to implement service fencing. If you select the default microservices namespace for a region from the application list, the applications that appear in the results do not belong to any microservices namespace.

**Create a microservices namespace**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > Microservice**
**Namespaces**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the **Microservice Namespaces** page, click **Create**
**Microservice Namespace**.
4. In the **Create Microservice Namespace** dialog box, set the parameters for the
microservices namespace and then click **Create**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Microservice Namespace | Enter a name for the microservices namespace that you want to create. |
| Microservice Namespace ID | Enter a string to specify the ID of the microservices namespace. The ID can contain only letters and digits. |
| Registration And Configuration Center | Dedicated Registry and Configuration Center Select a Dedicated Registry Instance. For more information, see Manage dedicated registries and configuration centers. Shared Registry and Configuration Center MSE Nacos: The Microservice Engine (MSE) Nacos engine that you purchased. The Nacos engine can be seamlessly integrated with EDAS for service registration and configuration management. EDAS Registration and Configuration Center: A free service registration and configuration center provided by EDAS. If your application requires high performance and stability, use MSE Nacos as the service registration and configuration center. |

anagement for ECS clusters

| Region | The region to which the microservices namespace belongs. You cannot change this parameter. |
|---|---|
| Allow Remote Debugging | To interconnect on-premises and cloud applications, go to the edit page for the microservices namespace of the application and turn on Allow Remote Debugging. For more information about debugging these applications, see the EDAS User Guide's Overview of the interconnection between on-premises and cloud applications chapter. |
| Description | Enter a description for the microservices namespace. |

**Edit a microservices namespace**

1. In the microservices namespace list, find the microservices namespace that you want to
edit and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
2. In the **Edit Microservice Namespace** dialog box, modify the **Microservice Namespace**
name and **Description**. You can also enable or disable the remote debugging feature. When you are finished, click **OK**.

**Delete a microservices namespace**

You can delete a microservices namespace only if the following prerequisites are met: No clusters belong to the microservices namespace. No microservice applications belong to the microservices namespace. No Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances belong to the microservices namespace.
1. In the microservices namespace list, find the microservices namespace that you want to
delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.
2. In the **Confirm** dialog box, click **Delete**.

#### ECS cluster management

##### Create an ECS cluster in the console

An Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) ECS cluster provides a deployment environment for your applications. To host applications in an EDAS ECS environment, you must first create an ECS cluster. This topic describes how to create an Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster.

**Prerequisites**

If you want to create an ECS cluster in a virtual private cloud (VPC), ensure that you have created a VPC. For more information, see the *VPC User Guide* > Set up a VPC with an
**IPv4 CIDR block** section.
If you have high security requirements for your resources and services, you can create a microservices namespace for isolation. For more information, see Manage microservices namespaces in the console.

**Background information**

EDAS provides two types of ECS clusters: Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters and non-Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters (hybrid cloud ECS clusters). Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster: A cluster that consists of Alibaba Cloud ECS instances. Non-Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster: A hybrid cloud cluster that can contain Alibaba Cloud ECS instances, servers in on-premises data centers, and servers from other cloud service providers. These servers are connected through leased lines and added to a non-Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster in EDAS for centralized management. For more information about non-Alibaba Cloud ECS clusters, see Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the EDAS console.
anagement for ECS clusters
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS**
**Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, select a region from the top menu bar, select a
**Microservices Namespace**, and then click **Create Cluster**.
You can select the microservices namespace on this page or in the **Create Cluster** dialog box. If you require environment isolation, select the microservices namespace that you created. If you do not require environment isolation, select the **Default** microservices namespace.
4. In the **Create Cluster** dialog box, set the cluster parameters and then click **Create**.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Cluster Name | The cluster name can contain only letters, digits, underscores ( ), and _ periods (.). The name must be no more than 64 characters in length. |
| Cluster Ownership | Alibaba Cloud: An Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster. Non-Alibaba Cloud: A non-Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster, also known as a hybrid cloud cluster. A hybrid cloud cluster can connect Alibaba Cloud ECS instances, servers in an on-premises data center, or servers from other cloud service providers through a leased line. These servers are then added to the Non-Alibaba Cloud cluster. For more information, see Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster. |
| Cluster Type | Only ECS is supported. |
| Cluster Network Type | Only VPC is supported. |
| VPC | After you select VPC, select a specific VPC. |
| Microservices Namespace | The microservices namespace to which the cluster belongs. By default, this is the namespace selected on the ECS Clusters page. If no namespace is selected, the Default microservices namespace is displayed. Select a namespace as needed. |

After the cluster is created, a **Creation successful** message is displayed at the top of the page. The new cluster appears in the cluster list.

**What to do next**

After the cluster is created, it is empty. You must add ECS instances to the cluster. For more information, see Scale out an ECS cluster in the console.

##### Scale out an ECS cluster using the console

After you create an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster, the cluster is empty and does not contain any ECS instances. You must add instances to the cluster. You may also need to scale out the cluster to accommodate business growth. In both cases, you need to import ECS instances into the cluster.

**Background information**

The import method varies based on the network type and operating system of the ECS instance that you want to add.

**Important**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) does not support Windows-based ECS instances. anagement for ECS clusters

**Add existing ECS instances**

If you already have ECS instances, you can add them to your ECS cluster. There are three ways to add existing ECS instances: Direct import: Does not require image conversion. Import after conversion: Reinstalls the operating system using an official EDAS image. After the reinstallation, all data on the instance is deleted, and you must set a new logon password for the instance. You cannot directly import an ECS instance if any of the following conditions are met: The instance was created before December 1, 2017. The instance is in the classic network and is being imported into a cluster that also uses the classic network. The instance is not in the Running state. For example, it is in the Stopped, Starting, or Stopping state.

**Note**

For instances that require conversion, you can choose to import them by manually running a script if you do not want to reinstall the operating system. Import after manually running a script: To import an Ubuntu-based ECS instance from the classic network into an ECS cluster, you must log on to the instance and run a script. This method does not reinstall the operating system of the ECS instance.

**Add existing ECS instances**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, select a region in the top menu bar, select a
**Microservices Namespace**, and then click the ID of the target ECS cluster.
4. On the **Cluster Details** page, in the upper-right corner of the **ECS Instance** section, click
**Add Existing ECS**.
5. On the **Add ECS Instance** page, select an import method and ECS instances from the
instance list, and then click **Next**.
**Import ECS**: The microservices namespace and destination cluster cannot be
configured. You can select available ECS instances from the current microservices namespace to import into the cluster.

**Note**

If no eligible instances are available, click **Create ECS Instance** to open the **Elastic**
**Compute Service** purchase page and purchase new ECS instances.
anagement for ECS clusters
**Select From Existing Cluster**: Select a microservices namespace and a source cluster
in the region. Then, select instances from the **All ECS** list and add them to the **Selected**
**ECS** list.
6. On the **Ready To Import** page, verify the import method for each instance.
Direct import: On the **Ready To Import** tab, select the instances and click **Confirm And**
**Import**.
Import after conversion: On the **Ready To Import** tab, review the information for the selected instances. Select **I Agree To Convert The Preceding Instances That Need**

**To Be Imported, And I Understand That The Data In The Original System Will Be**

**Lost After The Conversion**. Set a new logon password for the ECS instances, and then
click **Confirm And Import**. Import after manually running a script: a. On the **Ready To Import** tab, copy the **Script Content**. b. Log on to the ECS instance that you want to import as the **root** user. c. Paste and run the script on the ECS instance.
7. On the **Importing** tab, view the import status of the instances.
After the instances are imported, return to the Cluster Details page. If **Running** is displayed in the **Health Check** column for an instance, the instance has been successfully imported.

**Remove an ECS instance**

1. On the **Cluster Details** page, in the **ECS Instance** section, find the instance that you want
to remove and click **Remove** in the **Actions** column.
2. In the **Remove ECS Instance** dialog box, confirm the information for the instance to be
removed, and click **Remove**. After the ECS instance is removed, it is deleted from the instance list. anagement for ECS clusters

**FAQ**

**What do I do if I cannot find an ECS instance that I created in the ECS console**

**when I try to import it into a cluster?**

1. Check whether the account used to create the ECS instance in the ECS console is the same
as the account used to log on to the EDAS console.
2. Check whether the created ECS instance and the cluster are in the same region.
3. Log on to the EDAS console. In the navigation pane, choose **Resource Management >**
**ECS**. On the **ECS** page, click **Import ECS** in the upper-right corner. On the **Select Cluster**
**And Existing ECS Instances** tab, click **Sync ECS**.

**Important**

Make sure that the operating system of your ECS instance is a version that is supported on the **Select Cluster And Existing ECS Instances** page.
4. If the ECS instance still does not appear in the EDAS console after you complete these
checks, contact technical support.

##### Scale out an ECS cluster using an API

This topic describes how to use the Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) SDK for Java to call an API and scale out an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster.

**Prerequisites**

Before you scale out an ECS cluster, complete the following preparations: Install the EDAS SDK for Java. For more information, see the **EDAS Developer Guide** . Determine the region where the ECS cluster was created. Create ECS instances. For example, the instance IDs are i-bp13o01lzmbsvhsl**** and i-bp13 o01lzmbsvhsl****. Create an ECS cluster. For more information, see Create an ECS cluster using an API. If you have already created an ECS cluster, you can call the ListCluster operation to query the list of clusters and obtain the cluster ID ( **ClusterId**) of your target cluster. For example, the cluster ID is 369d06d7-450b-4f3d-bf75-9536fcd9****.

**Background information**

You can call the InstallAgent or InsertClusterMember API operation to import ECS instances into an ECS cluster. We recommend that you use the InstallAgent API operation instead of the InsertClusterMember API operation. When you call the InsertClusterMember operation to import an ECS instance, the operating system of the instance is reinstalled. After the reinstallation, all data on the instance is deleted, and you must set a new logon password for the instance. For this reason, we do not recommend using this operation to import ECS instances. When you call the InstallAgent operation to import an ECS instance, the operating system of the instance is not reinstalled. For this reason, we recommend using this operation to import ECS instances. anagement for ECS clusters

**Scale out by adding existing ECS instances**

The following code shows how to import existing ECS instances into an ECS cluster.

```java
import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ServerException; import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile; import com.aliyuncs.edas.model.v20170801.InstallAgentRequest; import com.aliyuncs.edas.model.v20170801.InstallAgentResponse; public class InstallAgent {
    public static void main(String[] args)  {
        // The AccessKey ID of your Alibaba Cloud account or RAM user.
        String aliyun_user_ak = "<yourAccessKeyId>";
        // The AccessKey secret of your Alibaba Cloud account or RAM user.
        String aliyun_user_sk = "<yourAccessKeySecret>";
        // The ID of the region where the cluster resides.
        String region_id = "cn-hangzhou";
        DefaultProfile defaultProfile = DefaultProfile.getProfile(region_id,
aliyun_user_ak, aliyun_user_sk);
        DefaultAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(defaultProfile);
        // Create an API request and set its parameters.
        InstallAgentRequest request = new InstallAgentRequest();
        // The ID of the target ECS cluster.
        request.setClusterId("369d06d7-450b-4f3d-bf75-9536fcd9****");
        // The IDs of the ECS instances to import. Separate multiple instance IDs with
commas (,).
```

##### Manage ECS clusters

This topic describes how to view, manage, and delete Elastic Compute Service (ECS) clusters. It also describes how to manage the ECS instances and applications in the clusters.

**Prerequisites**

An ECS cluster has been created. For more information, see Create an ECS cluster in the console.

**View cluster information**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS**
**Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Cluster** page, select a region from the top menu bar and a
**Microservices Namespace** from the top of the page.
4. In the cluster list, you can view information such as **Cluster ID/Name**, **VPC ID/Network**
**Type**, **Cluster Type**, **Number of Instances**, **Resources**, **Remaining Resources**,
**Cluster Status**, **Microservices Namespace**, and **Creation Time**.
anagement for ECS clusters
5. In the cluster list, click **Edit** in the Actions column. In the **Edit Cluster Name** dialog box,
edit the **Cluster Name** and click **OK**. In the cluster list, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column, then in the **Confirm** dialog box, click
**OK** to delete the destination cluster.
6. Click the cluster ID to go to the **Cluster Details** page. You can view **Cluster Information**,
manage **ECS Instances**, and view the **Application List**.

| Area | Description | Related operations |
|---|---|---|
| Cluster information | Basic information about this cluster, such as Cluster Owner, Cluster ID, Cluster Name, Microservices Namespace, Cluster Type, VPC ID, Network Type, Cluster Status, and Description, and so on. | Click Edit to modify the cluster description. Click View Details to view the details of the cluster. |
| ECS Instances | This section displays the ECS instances in this cluster and their basic information. You can manage the ECS instances in the current cluster. In the instance list, you can view information such as Instance ID/Name, IP Address, Instance Type, Health Check, Deployed Applications, and Join Time. | For more information, see Manage cluster instances. |
| Application List | The list of applications in the cluster. You can view information such as Application Name, JDK Version, Application Runtime Environment, Total Instances, Running Instances, and Owner. | Click the application name to go to the application's Basic Information page. |

**Manage cluster instances**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS**
**Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Cluster** page, select a region from the top menu bar and a
**Microservices Namespace** from the top of the page.
4. Click the Cluster ID to go to the **Cluster Details** page.
anagement for ECS clusters
5. On the **Cluster Details** page, in the **ECS Instances** section, you can search by **Health**
**Check**, **Application Deployment Status**, and **Instance ID/name**. In the instance list,
you can view **Instance ID/name**, **IP Address**, **Instance Type**, **Health Check**, **Deployed**
**Applications**, and **Time Joined the Cluster**.

| Feature | Operation |
|---|---|
| Add existing ECS | In the upper-right corner of the ECS instances section, select Add existing ECS to add existing ECS instances to the current cluster. For detailed steps, see the Add existing ECS section. |
| View ECS instance details | In the ECS instances section, for an ECS instance with deployed applications, click View details in the Operation column to view basic application information. |
| View deployed application details for an ECS instance | In the Deployed applications column, click a specific application name to go to the Basic information page for that application. |
| Remove ECS instance | If the Health Check status of an ECS instance isO ffline, you can remove the ECS instance from the cluster. Remove a single instance: a. In the Operation column for an ECS instance with nod eployed applications, click Remove. b. In the Remove ECS instance dialog box, click Remove. Remove multiple instances: a. In the ECS instance list, select multiple running ECS instances with no deployed applications using the checkboxes on the left. Then, in the ECS instances section, click Batch remove. b. In the Confirm dialog box, click OK. |
| Transfer ECS instance to another cluster | You can transfer ECS instances in bulk without deployed applications to another cluster. i. Select multiple ECS instances without deployed applications using the checkboxes on the left of the ECS instance list. Then, in the ECS instances section, click Transfer ECS instance. ii. In the Select destination cluster tab, select a microservices namespace and destination cluster, then click Next. iii. In the Prepare import tab, click Confirm and import. Note If the instance cannot be imported directly, select I agree to convert the instances listed above for import and understand that existing system data will be lost after conversion, then set a new logon password for the ECS instance. |

**Delete Cluster**

anagement for ECS clusters
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS**
**Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, in the cluster list, verify that the **Number of instances**
for the destination cluster is 0. To view the cluster list, see View cluster information. If the number of instances is 0, proceed to step 4. If the number of instances is not 0, remove the ECS instances from the cluster first. For more information, see Remove ECS instances.
4. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, in the cluster list, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column for
the destination cluster.

**Important**

You cannot delete a cluster if it contains instances.
5. In the **Confirm** dialog box, click **OK**.

**References**

For more information, see Create an ECS cluster using the console and Scale out an ECS cluster using the console.

##### Manage instance groups for an application

**in an ECS cluster using the console**

You can group the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances of an application to deploy different versions of the application to different groups. You can also manage traffic and perform phased releases based on instance groups.

**Overview of instance groups**

For example, the itemcenter application is deployed on 10 ECS instances. These instances are divided into two groups: the **Default Group** and the **Beta Group**. The **Default Group** contains six instances, and the **Beta Group** contains four instances. The application now has two instance groups, which lets you deploy different application versions to each group.

**Note**

When you create an application in Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS), a **Default Group** is automatically created for the application. This group cannot be deleted. If you do not need to manage traffic or perform a phased release for multi-version deployments, use the **Default Group**. No other groups are required.

**Create a group**

If you want to verify a new application version without affecting traffic in the production environment, you can perform a phased release. To do this, create a new group for the application.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Management > Applications**.
anagement for ECS clusters
3. Select a region from the top menu bar and a **Microservices Namespace** from the top of
the page. Then, on the **Application List** page, click an application name.
4. On the application details page, click the **Instance Information** tab. Then click **Create**
**Group** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Create Group** dialog box, enter a **Group Name**, select a **Deployment Package**
**Version**, and click **Create**.
After the group is created, a **The group is created.** message is displayed at the top of the page.

**Modify a group name**

1. After the group is created, click the edit icon
next to the group name.
2. In the **Edit** dialog box, modify the **Group Name** and click **Confirm**.

**Add an instance**

After you create a group, you can add instances to the group by **scaling out the**
**application** or **changing the group** of an existing instance. The procedures are as follows:

**Method 1: Scale out the application**

For instructions on adding instances to a group using **Application Scale-out**, see Scale out an application.

**Method 2: Change the group**

You can use the **Change Group** feature to move instances to the new group.
1. On the **Instance Information** tab, find the instance that you want to move, and in the
**Actions** column, click **Change Group**.
2. In the **Change Group** dialog box, select a **Target Group**, confirm the information, select a
deployment policy, and click **OK**. The relationships among groups, instances, and application versions are complex. If you select **No Application Version Is Deployed** for the new group, the application version of the current instance, such as V1.0, becomes the default deployment version for the new group. If **An Application Version Is Already Deployed** to the new group, such as V2.0, and this version is different from the one on the current instance, such as V1.0, the **Change**
**Group** dialog box displays both versions. You can select a deployment policy as needed.
To deploy the application version (V2.0) from the new group to the instance, select **Re-**
**deploy The Current Instance By Using The Version Of The Target Group**.
To keep the instance's currently deployed application version (V1.0), select **Change**
**Group Only, Without Redeployment**.

**Note**

A message appears if the deployment package version of the instance is different from the version of its group.

**View groups**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Management > Applications**.
anagement for ECS clusters
3. On the application details page, click the **Instance Information** tab to view the
application's group information and the deployment package version in each group. The group information includes the following details: If an application is deployed to the group, the last deployed package version is displayed next to the group name. The application instances are listed under the groups to which they belong.

**Set JVM and Tomcat parameters for a group**

You can configure JVM and Tomcat parameters for an instance group or for an entire application. For more information, see Configure JVM parameters and Configure Tomcat.
1. On the **Instance Information** tab of the application details page, click **Group Settings**
next to the desired group.
2. From the drop-down list, click **JVM** or **Tomcat**. In the dialog box that appears, click
**Confirm**.
3. In the **Group Settings** (JVM or Tomcat) dialog box, set the parameters, and click
**Configure JVM Parameters** or **Configure Tomcat**.
For more information about JVM and Tomcat parameters, see Configure JVM parameters and Configure Tomcat.

**Bind an SLB instance to a group**

For information about the scenarios and the detailed procedure for binding a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance to a group, see the **Server Load Balancer Overview** chapter in the
**EDAS User Guide**.

**Delete a group**

If a group contains no instances and you no longer need it, you can delete the group. This operation cannot be undone. Proceed with caution.
1. On the **Instance Information** tab of the application details page, click the **Delete Group**
button.
2. In the **Delete Group** dialog box, click **Delete**.

##### Manage application instance groups in an

**ECS cluster using APIs**

This topic describes how to use the Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) software development kit (SDK) for Java to call APIs to manage application instance groups in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster.

**Prerequisites**

Before you manage application instance groups in an ECS cluster, ensure that the following prerequisites are met: Install the EDAS SDK for Java. For more information, see the EDAS Developer Guide. Identify the region where the application is located. For example, the region is cnhangzhou. Before you create an application instance group, call the ListHistoryDeployVersion operation to query the deployment package version history of the application and obtain the ID of the target version (PackageVersion.Id). anagement for ECS clusters Before you change the group of an ECS instance, call the ListApplicationEcc operation to query the Elastic Compute Container (ECC) information for the application and obtain the ECC ID of the target ECS instance (EccId). Create ECS instances. For example, the instance IDs are i-bp13o01lzmbsvhsl**** and i-bp13 o01lzmbsvhsl****. Create an ECS cluster. For more information, see Create an ECS cluster using an API. If you already have an ECS cluster, you can call the ListCluster operation to query the clusters and obtain the ID of the target ECS cluster (ClusterId). For example, the cluster ID is 369d06d7-450b-4f3d-bf75-9536fcd9****.

**Background information**

You can group the ECS instances of an application. This lets you deploy different application versions in different groups. You can use application instance groups to manage traffic and perform phased releases.

#### ECS instance management

##### Install EDAS Agent on an ECS instance

The Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) Agent is a daemon program that runs on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance to manage communication between an EDAS cluster and the applications on the instance. You must install the EDAS Agent on an ECS instance before you can deploy an application to it in EDAS.

**Background information**

EDAS deploys applications only to ECS instances that have the EDAS Agent installed. Application deployment includes initial installation and scale-out. In EDAS, an application instance is an ECS instance that has the EDAS Agent installed and an application deployed. If you want to use an existing ECS instance in EDAS, you must first install the EDAS Agent on it. The EDAS Agent provides the following features: Application lifecycle management: Deploys, starts, and stops applications. Status reporting: Reports the application liveness status, health check status, and Ali- Tomcat container status. Information retrieval: Retrieves monitoring information from ECS instances and containers. The EDAS Agent facilitates communication between the EDAS console and your application. The agent helps ensure that your application is deployed correctly and promptly to an ECS instance. The EDAS Agent supports 64-bit CentOS 6.5 and later.

**Note**

You do not need to manage these features. You only need to install the EDAS Agent. anagement for ECS clusters EDAS provides two methods to install the EDAS Agent: Automatically install the EDAS Agent by importing an ECS instance Manually install the EDAS Agent using a command script

**Important**

By default, the EDAS Agent is installed with Java Development Kit (JDK) 8. If you want to use JDK 7 or another version, you must install the EDAS Agent using a command script. To use the script, you must log on to your ECS instance as the **root** user. You can run the script multiple times. Each time you run the script, it overwrites the existing EDAS Agent installation. The EDAS Agent does not have a separate update script. To update the EDAS Agent, run the installation script again. The installation script is region-specific. Switch to the region of your ECS instance, and then click **Install Agent**. The agent status varies based on the image and cluster type that you select. The agent status determines the application types that you can deploy on the ECS instance. Follow the instructions for your chosen installation method.

**Automatically install EDAS Agent by importing an ECS instance**

If you did not select the **EDAS JAVA Environment (Common ECS)** base image when you purchased your ECS instance, you can install the EDAS Agent using the **Import ECS** feature in the EDAS console. This feature lets you import an ECS instance either directly or after a conversion. An ECS instance cannot be imported directly if it meets any of the following conditions: The instance was created before December 1, 2017. The instance is in a classic network and is being imported to a cluster that uses a classic network. The instance is stopped, starting, or stopping. The instance is a Windows-based instance or does not support simple Shell commands. The instance is not imported from another ECS cluster.

**Important**

If image conversion is required, the ECS instance is formatted. If you do not want to anagement for ECS clusters format the disks, install the EDAS Agent using a command script.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > ECS**.
3. On the **ECS** page, select a region from the top menu bar and a microservices namespace
(optional), and then click **Import ECS** in the upper-right corner.
4. On the **Select Cluster And Existing ECS Instances** tab in the **Import ECS** wizard, select
a **Microservices Namespace** and a **Select Destination Cluster**. From the instance list, select the ECS instance to import and click **Next**.

**Note**

If you do not have a destination cluster, click **Create Cluster** next to the **Select**
**Destination Cluster** drop-down list.
To perform a manual installation, click **Switch To Manual Installation** in the upper-right corner of the page. You are then redirected to the **Manually Install**
**EDAS Agent On Single Instance** page, where you can use a command script
to install the EDAS Agent.
5. On the **Ready To Import** tab, review the instance information.
For instances listed under **The Following Instances Can Be Imported Directly**
**Without Conversion**, click **Confirm And Import**.
anagement for ECS clusters For instances in the **The Following Instances Need To Be Imported After**
**Conversion** section, select **I Agree To Convert The Preceding Instances That Need**

**To Be Imported, And I Understand That The Data In The Original System Will Be**

**Lost After The Conversion**. Enter a new logon password for the root user and click
**Confirm And Import**.
6. On the **Import** tab, you can view the import status of the instance.
For instances that can be imported directly: The **Import** page displays the import status. If the **The Instance Is Transferred** message is displayed, the instance has been imported. Click **Back To Cluster Details**. The instance is successfully imported into the cluster when its status changes to **Running**. For an instance that requires conversion, the **Import** page shows the import status as
**Converting. It Might Take 5 Minutes**. If you click **Back To Cluster Details** before the
import is complete, the health check status is **Converting** and a progress percentage is displayed. When the import is complete, the health check status changes to **Running**.

**Manually install EDAS Agent using a command script**

You can use this method only for ECS instances that are in an ECS cluster.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > ECS**.
3. On the **ECS** page, select a region from the top menu bar, select a microservices
namespace, and then click **Import ECS** in the upper-right corner.
4. On the **Import ECS** page, click **Switch To Manual Installation** in the upper-right corner.
The **Manually Install EDAS Agent On Single Instance** page appears. Click **Copy**. anagement for ECS clusters

**Note**

To install using an image, click **Back** in the upper-right corner to return to the configuration page, where you can complete the import. For more information, see Automatically install EDAS Agent by importing an ECS instance.
5. Log on to the ECS instance as the **root** user.
6. On the ECS instance, paste and run the copied command.

**Verify the result**

1. After you install the EDAS Agent, go to the EDAS console. In the navigation pane on the left,
choose **Resource Management** > **ECS**.
2. On the **ECS** page, select the destination region from the top menu bar and a microservices
namespace. You can then view the status in the **Agent Status** column. A status of **Online** or **Online Docker** indicates that the EDAS Agent is installed. If the installation fails, the status is **Unknown**.

**Update EDAS Agent**

The procedure to update the EDAS Agent is the same as the procedure to install it using a command script. For more information, see Manually install the EDAS Agent using a command script.

#### Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster

**Background information**

Your application system may have the following requirements or face the following challenges: Traffic on Alibaba Cloud is volatile, and you may face traffic spikes. Although you can predict traffic volumes, the predictions may not be accurate. This makes it difficult to determine when to perform scale-outs and how many ECS instances are required. As a result, you must purchase ECS instances in advance. Some core business systems have high security requirements, and you want to deploy these applications in your own on-premises data center (IDC). However, you cannot centrally manage applications that are deployed in different environments because the networks for Alibaba Cloud ECS instances, servers in your IDC, and servers from other cloud service providers are not interconnected. To meet your business and availability requirements, you want to deploy your applications in a hybrid cloud environment. However, you cannot centrally manage these applications. This process requires manual intervention, which can lead to operational errors.

**Step 1: Create a hybrid cloud cluster**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > EDAS ECS**
**Clusters**.
3. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, select a region from the top menu bar. Then, select a
microservices namespace and click **Create Cluster**. You can select a microservices namespace on this page or in the **Create Cluster** dialog box. anagement for ECS clusters If environment isolation is required, select the microservices namespace that you created. If environment isolation is not required, you can select the **Default** microservices namespace.
4. In the **Create Cluster** dialog box, set the cluster parameters and then click **Create**.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Cluster Name | The cluster name can contain only letters, digits, underscores ( ), and _ periods (.). The name can be up to 64 characters in length. |
| Cluster Affiliation | Select Non-Alibaba Cloud. |
| Cluster Type | This parameter is set to ECS and cannot be changed. |
| Cluster Network Type | For a Non-Alibaba Cloud ECS cluster, the network type can only beV PC. |
| VPC | After you select VPC, you must select a specific VPC that you have created. |
| Microservices Namespace | The microservices namespace to which the cluster belongs. By default, this parameter is set to the microservices namespace that you selected on the ECS Clusters page. If you did not select a namespace, Default microservices namespace is displayed. Select a namespace as needed. |

After the cluster is created, a **Creation Successful** message is displayed at the top of the page, and the new cluster appears in the cluster list.

**Note**

The created cluster is an empty cluster. You must add Alibaba Cloud ECS instances and servers from your on-premises data center to the cluster.

**Step 2: Add instances to the hybrid cloud cluster**

You must add Alibaba Cloud ECS instances, servers from your on-premises data center, and servers from other cloud service providers to the empty hybrid cloud cluster.
1. On the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page, click the ID of the cluster that you created.
2. On the **Cluster Details** page, in the upper-right corner of the **ECS Instance** section, click
**Add Existing ECS**.
3. In the **Add ECS Instance** dialog box, copy the EDAS Agent installation command.
anagement for ECS clusters

**Note**

To add instances to a hybrid cloud cluster, you must manually install EDAS Agent on the instances using the command line.
4. Log on to your Alibaba Cloud ECS instance or a server in your on-premises data center as
the root user. Then, paste and run the EDAS Agent installation command. After the command is run, the instance or server is added to the cluster.

**Verify the result**

1. Return to the **EDAS ECS Clusters** page. In the cluster list, check the **Cluster Type**,
**Cluster Status**, and **Instances** values for the new cluster.
If the **Cluster Type** is **ECS Cluster (Non-Alibaba Cloud)** and the **Cluster Status** is
**Normal**, the cluster was created successfully.
If the value in the **Instances** column is the same as the number of instances that you added, the instances were added successfully.
2. Click the cluster ID to go to the cluster details page. In the **ECS Instance** section, view the
names and the **Health Check** status of the added instances. If the **Health Check** status of an instance is **Running**, the instance is running correctly.

**What to do next**

After you create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster, you can deploy applications to it. The deployment method is the same as that for a standard ECS cluster. For more information, see Application creation and deployment overview (ECS).

#### Sync VPC

A virtual private cloud (VPC) is a custom private network built on Alibaba Cloud. VPCs are logically isolated from each other. This service is ideal for users who require high network security and have some network management experience. A VPC that you create in the VPC console automatically syncs to the EDAS console, but with a short delay. You can manually sync a VPC to avoid delays that may affect your operations.

**Prerequisites**

Before you sync a VPC in EDAS, make sure you have created a VPC in the VPC console. For details, see the **VPC User Guide > Create and manage a VPC** topic.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Resource Management > VPC**.
3. On the **VPC** page, select a region from the top menu bar. Then, in the upper-right corner,
click **Synchronize VPC**.
4. After the VPC is synced, you can view its details in the EDAS console.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

anagement for ECS clusters

| VPC ID | It is automatically generated upon VPC creation. |
|---|---|
| Name | You define this name when you create the VPC. |
| IPv4 CIDR block | The IPv4 CIDR block that you set when you create the VPC. |
| IPv6 CIDR block | The IPv6 CIDR block that you set when you create the VPC. |
| Status | A VPC has one of two statuses: active or configuring. |

#### Manage resource groups

If you use an Alibaba Cloud account to purchase resources and use Resource Access Management (RAM) users for application operations and maintenance (O&M), you can use resource groups to manage permissions. EDAS lets you grant a RAM user permissions on a specific resource group. The RAM user can then manage all resources within that resource group. For more information, see Permission management overview.

**Note**

In Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS), a resource group is used to classify resources. You can bind Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances, Server Load Balancer (SLB) instances, and clusters to a resource group. However, you cannot bind Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) to a resource group.

**Common scenarios**

A company uses EDAS to deploy its business applications. Department A is responsible for User Center applications, and Department B is responsible for Product Hub applications. The two departments use the same Alibaba Cloud account for EDAS, and each department has a RAM user. Department A uses dedicated ECS and SLB instances to deploy its User Center applications. The company creates a resource group in EDAS, adds the ECS and SLB instances for Department A to the resource group, and then grants the RAM user for Department A permissions on that resource group. The RAM user for Department A can only manage the resources in this resource group and cannot manage the resources of Department B. This prevents operational conflicts between the two departments. anagement for ECS clusters

the region and the ECS and SLB instances in each resource group.

### Create and deploy

**applications**

#### Overview of Application Creation and

**Deployment (ECS)**

In an EDAS ECS cluster, you can create and deploy applications using Java microservice frameworks. anagement for ECS clusters

**Applications**

An EDAS ECS cluster supports mainstream Java microservice frameworks such as Spring Cloud and Dubbo. It also supports Alibaba's proprietary HSF and Alibaba Application Server.

**Note**

To help you quickly try application creation and deployment, EDAS provides sample applications for various microservice frameworks.

**ECS environments**

EDAS offers two types of ECS environments: Alibaba Cloud ECS and hybrid cloud ECS. An Alibaba Cloud ECS environment uses resources provided entirely by Alibaba Cloud. These include a microservices namespace, VPC, ECS cluster, and ECS instances. Create a microservices namespace, VPC, ECS cluster, and ECS instances as needed. A hybrid cloud ECS environment mainly uses instances from Alibaba Cloud ECS, onpremises data centers, and other cloud service providers to host applications. However, the microservices namespace, VPC, and ECS cluster are still created in Alibaba Cloud.

**Creation and deployment**

Create and deploy applications in the appropriate ECS environment as needed. Different frameworks support different plan types. Each plan type requires a specific application runtime environment. Deployment package type anagement for ECS clusters Spring Cloud and Dubbo applications support JAR and WAR plan types. HSF applications support only WAR. Alibaba Application Server is used for J2EE application deployment. Application runtime environments For Spring Cloud and Dubbo applications deployed using a JAR file, select the standard Java environment. For Spring Cloud and Dubbo applications deployed using a WAR file, select Apache Tomcat as the application runtime environment. For HSF applications—which support only WAR deployment—select EDAS-Container as the application runtime environment. EDAS-Container includes Ali-Tomcat and Pandora. For J2EE applications, select Alibaba Application Server as the application runtime environment. An ECS cluster supports application creation and deployment through both the console and APIs.

**Scenarios**

During your first deployment, choose a deployment method based on your scenario. Then follow the related documentation to create and deploy your application. Quickly try application creation and deployment Deploy a sample application to an ECS environment. The ECS environment includes a microservices namespace, VPC, and cluster. For step-by-step instructions, see Deploy a Java microservice application in an ECS environment. Alibaba Cloud deployment Deploy an existing application to an Alibaba Cloud ECS environment. For step-by-step instructions, see Create and deploy an application in an ECS cluster. Hybrid cloud deployment Deploy an existing application to a hybrid cloud ECS environment. For step-by-step instructions, see Deploy an application in a hybrid cloud.

**Configure an Internet-facing SLB instance**

Applications are typically created and deployed in a VPC. By default, these applications do not have a public IP address. To allow access to your application from the Internet, you must configure an Internet-facing SLB instance.

**Note**

EDAS sets the HTTP listeners for managed applications to use session persistence. This setting cannot be changed.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. Then, select a
**microservices namespace** and an **ECS cluster** from the top of the page. Click the name
of the target application.

**Settings** section, click **Load Balancing (Internet)**, and then click **Add** on the right.
5. In the **Add SLB and Application Binding** dialog box, configure the load balancing
parameters. For more information, see Dedicated SLB instance for an application. Copy the public IP address and port of the configured Internet-facing SLB instance, for example, `39.XX.XX.65:81` . Paste the address into your browser's address bar and press Enter to access your application's web page.

**ECS system configuration constraints**

After you create an application, you may need to log on to the ECS instance to perform system configurations. When you configure the system, you must adhere to the following constraints: Do not delete the admin user. Do not delete the /home/admin directory. Do not stop the following processes on the host: /home/staragent/bin/staragentd com.alibaba.edas.agent.AgentDaemon Do not delete the following crontab entries on the host: anagement for ECS clusters The bash /home/admin/edas-agent/bin/monitor.sh task for the root user The bash /home/admin/edas-agent/bin/rotator.sh task for the admin user Ensure that the root partition has free space. If you use CentOS, ensure that the yum repository is correctly configured and functional. If the ECS instance uses multiple NICs, such as when Docker is installed and the application is an HSF application, specify the **-Dhsf.server.ip** parameter for the application to ensure that the registered IP address is correct. For more information, see JVM -D startup configuration parameters. The clock on the ECS instance must be accurate. The maximum clock drift must not exceed 15 seconds. Otherwise, the application cannot access the EDAS registry.

**Deploy a tar.gz or zip package application in an ECS cluster**

**Environment preparation**

First, enable compressed package deployment in the EDAS database. Log on to the EDAS database and run the following SQL statement:

```
insert into edas_web_properties (pro_k,pro_v,env_tag,component) values("featureAppCompressEnable","true","*","*");
```

**Compressed package configuration**

The compressed package must contain start.sh and stop.sh files, and both files must be valid. Example of start.sh:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# auto inject by EDAS...
# source /home/admin/app/19049ac9-a7ce-469f-9f5c-7fb3d0181868/edas_env.sh
# auto inject by EDAS...
# Get the absolute path of the script
cd `dirname $0`
# The application deployment directory is automatically printed as a variable named CSL
during startup export CSL_DEPLOY_DIR=`pwd` export DEPLOY_DIR=`pwd`
# To use system environment variables together with prehook
# source /home/admin/test_env.sh
java $EDAS_ENV -jar sc-nacos-provider-G.jar
```

Example of stop.sh:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Get the PID of the application
PID=`ps -ef | grep -v "grep" | grep "start.sh" | awk '{print $2}'`
# Send the termination signal to the application
pkill -TERM $PID
```

**Deploy the application**

anagement for ECS clusters

**Note**

Compressed package deployment is disabled by default. Contact an O&M engineer to enable it.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar, and then a
**microservices namespace** from the top of the page. In the upper-left corner, click
**Create Application**.
4. On the **Application Basic Information** tab of the Create Application wizard, select **ECS**
**Cluster** as the Cluster Type and **Package Deployment** as the **Application Runtime**
**Environment**.
5. You can enter the **Application name** and click Next.
6. In the **Application Configuration** tab, select **Custom Program** as the deployment
package source, choose **Upload Compressed Package** as the file upload method, click
**Select File** next to Upload Compressed Package, and upload the .tar or .zip package you
want to deploy.
7. Set **Instance Source** to **Use Existing Instance** and **Environment** to **Custom**
**Environment**. Select a **Microservices Namespace** and a **Cluster**. For **Instance Source**
**Type**, select **Instances In The Current Cluster** and check the desired ECS instances.
Click **Next** at the bottom of the page. anagement for ECS clusters
8. On the **Advanced Settings** tab, configure the **Version**, **Application health check**,
**Batch**, **Batching method**, and **Agent version** parameters. Then, click **Create**
**application**.
9. On the **Application Creation Complete** tab, click the **Confirm and Create Application**
button at the bottom. On the **Basic Information** page, click **View details** in the notification at the top. On the
**Change Details** page, view the change process. The application deployment takes several
minutes to complete. After the deployment is complete, return to the **Basic Information** page and click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab to check the instance status. If the status is **Normal**, the application is deployed successfully.

**Monitoring and JVM parameters (optional)**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. Click the application name. On the **Basic Information** tab, edit the required parameters.
Then, add the $EDAS_ENV environment variable to the Java startup command in the start.sh script.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Application monitoring > Application**
**overview** to view monitoring information.

#### Deploy applications in hybrid cloud

**clusters**

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) lets you deploy applications in hybrid cloud Elastic Compute Service (ECS) clusters and provides comprehensive solutions for scale-out, networking, and centralized management for these clusters.

**Prerequisites**

You have subscribed to the **Professional Edition** or **Platinum Edition** of EDAS. You have created a hybrid cloud ECS cluster. For more information, see Create a hybrid cloud ECS cluster.

**Background information**

EDAS lets you deploy applications in hybrid cloud ECS clusters and provides comprehensive solutions for scale-out, networking, and centralized management for these clusters. You can connect Alibaba Cloud ECS instances, servers from on-premises data centers, and servers from other cloud service providers (CSPs) using leased lines. After you add these servers to a hybrid cloud ECS cluster in EDAS, you can host applications on the cluster.

**Deploy an application**

The procedure for deploying an application in a hybrid cloud ECS cluster is the same as for an ECS cluster. For more information, see Create and deploy an application in an ECS cluster.

### Update and roll back

**applications**

#### Overview of application upgrades and

**rollbacks (ECS)**

After you create and deploy an application in Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS), you will need to upgrade it over time. If an upgraded version has issues, you can roll the application back to a previous version. This topic describes the available upgrade policies and methods, and how to roll back an application.

**Upgrade an application**

anagement for ECS clusters The upgrade scenarios, policies, and methods vary depending on the status of the new application version.

| Upgrade policy | Scenario | Upgrade method | References |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-batch release (Direct upgrade) | If an application has a small number of instances or a simple service architecture, you can upgrade it directly after development and testing by deploying the new version. | Console API Plug-ins or tools | For more information, see: Create and deploy an application in an ECS cluster Use the CLI to quickly deploy an application to an ECS cluster Use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to upgrade an application (ECS cluster) Deploy an application in an ECS cluster using Cloud Toolkit in IntelliJ IDEA |
| Phased release | If an application has many instances or a complex service architecture, you can release it in multiple batches. The application is upgraded on only a few instances in each batch. The phased release is complete when the application is upgraded on all instances. If an error occurs during the phased release, you can stop the process and roll back the application. You can release the application again after the error is fixed. | Console API Plug-ins or tools | For more information, see: Release an application in phases using the console Use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to release an application in phases (ECS cluster) Use Cloud Toolkit to release an application in phases |
| Canary release | A new application version is first verified on a small number of instances. If the verification is successful, you can upgrade the application on all instances. | Console | For more information, see Release an application in canary mode using the console (ECS cluster). |

**Roll back an application**

If an error occurs during or after an application upgrade, you can roll the application back to its previous version. After you fix the error, you can upgrade the application again. Rollback during an upgrade: If an error occurs during the upgrade, you can stop the process and roll back the application. Rollback after an upgrade: If the upgrade is complete but you find an issue with the new version, you can roll back the application by deploying a previous version. For more information, see Use the console to roll back an application (ECS cluster). anagement for ECS clusters

#### At-a-time release (applicable to ECS

**clusters)**

##### Upgrade an application in an ECS cluster

**using the console**

This topic describes how to use the Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) console to upgrade an application in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster in a single batch.

**Background information**

In addition to using the console, you can also use Cloud Toolkit and the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to release an application in a single batch. For more information, see the following topics: Deploy an application using Cloud Toolkit in IntelliJ IDEA (ECS cluster) Use Cloud Toolkit in Eclipse to deploy an application to an ECS cluster Use the toolkit-maven-plugin to upgrade applications (ECS clusters)

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Management > Application List**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar, a microservices
namespace at the top of the page, and ECS Cluster from the cluster type list. Then, click the name of the target application in the application list.
4. In the upper-right corner of the **Instance Information** page, click **Deploy Application**.
5. On the **Deployment Mode Selection** page, in the upper-right corner of the **Regular**
**Release (Single/Multiple Batches)** area, click **Start Deployment**.
6. On the **Standard Release (Single/Multiple Batches)** page, set the deployment package
and related information for the new application version, set the **Release Policy**, and then click **OK**. anagement for ECS clusters i. Configure the deployment package and related information.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Enable Application Monitoring | If application monitoring is not enabled, features such as alert monitoring, trace query, microservice search, service authentication, outlier removal, graceful shutdown, and canary release will be unavailable. |
| Application Deployment Method | The deployment method is determined by how the application is first deployed. This method cannot be changed. For example, if an application is first deployed from a JAR package, subsequent upgrades must also use a JAR package. Note Use Historical Versions to roll back the application. For more information, see Roll back applications in ECS clusters using the console. |
| File Upload Method | The method used to upload the deployment package for the new application version. You can upload a JAR or WAR package, or specify the URL of a JAR or WAR package. The type of deployment package depends on the deployment package that is used when you deploy the application for the first time. Upload JAR Package or Upload WAR Package: Click Select File and select the new application deployment package from your local computer. JAR Package Address or WAR Package Address: If the new application package is already uploaded to a cloud service, such as Object Storage Service (OSS), enter its URL in the text box. |
| Version | The new application version. You can enter a version number or clickU se Timestamp As Version Number. |
| Description | The description of the new application version. |

anagement for ECS clusters ii. Set the release policy.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Group | The target group for the phased release. If the application has only one group, select All Groups from the list. The maximum number of instances for the application is shown in parentheses next to the group name. The list also includes Default Group, which is the same as All Groups. If the application has multiple groups, select the target group from the list. Note If you select All Groups, all instances in all groups of the application are upgraded based on the Batches Per Group setting. |
| Batches Per Group | The number of batches for the phased release in the selected group. For a single-batch release, select 1 Batch. |
| Batch Mode | For single-batch releases, the batching method is set to Automatic by default and cannot be changed. |
| Java Environment | Select as needed. |

iii. Click **OK**. After a single-batch release starts, you are automatically redirected to the **Change**
**Details** page. On the **Change Details** page, you can track the progress and status of
the release. For more information, see the View application changes section.

**Verify the result**

1. View change records.
i. On the application details page, in the navigation pane on the left, click **Change History**. ii. On the **Change History** page, verify that the status in the **Change Status** column is
**Execution Successful**.
If the status is **Execution Successful**, the release is successful. If the status is **Execution Failed**, the release failed. In the **Actions** column, click **View** to check the change details and identify the cause of the failure.
2. View application details.
i. On the application details page, in the navigation pane on the left, click **Basic**
**Information**.
anagement for ECS clusters ii. Click the **Basic Information** tab, and in the **Application Information** area of the **Basic**
**Information** tab, check whether the application's **Deployment Package** is the
upgraded deployment package. iii. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, check whether the **Running Status** of each instance in the target group is **Normal**.

##### Use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to

**update an application in an ECS cluster**

You can use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to update Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and High-Speed Service Framework (HSF) applications that are deployed in Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS).

**Background information**

The toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in is an open-source tool that helps you build a complete lifecycle framework and set up a deployment environment for a project. You can also use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to update an application that is deployed in a Kubernetes cluster in EDAS. For more information, see Use the Cloud Toolkit plug-in to deploy an application in a single batch for Kubernetes.

**Procedure**

1. Add the dependency for toolkit-maven-plugin to the pom.xml file in your local application
project.

```xml
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>com.alibaba.cloud</groupId>
            <artifactId>toolkit-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>1.1.5</version>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

2. Create the `.edas_config.yaml` configuration file in the project's root directory, and
configure the deployment parameters in the file. A file whose name starts with a period ( `.` ) is a default configuration file for the IDE. If you do not specify another configuration file, the plug-in uses the `.edas_config.yaml` file in the root directory by default.

| start with a period | ( . |   |
|---|---|---|
| -Dedas config=xxx _ |   |   |
|   |   | pa |

If you create a configuration file whose name does not start with a period ( `.` ), you can specify it when you package the project by setting the `-Dedas_config=xxx` parameter. anagement for ECS clusters If a default configuration file exists and you also specify another configuration file using a parameter, the plug-in uses the specified configuration file.

**Note**

If the current project is a submodule of a Maven project, the default configuration file must be stored in the root directory of the submodule, not the root directory of the parent Maven project. The following examples show configurations for typical update scenarios:

**Update all instance groups of an application**

For example, you have an application with the ID `eb20****-e6ee-4f6d-a36f-` `5f6a5455****` in the China (Beijing) region, and you need to upgrade all application groups. The following code shows a configuration example:

```
env:
     region_id: cn-beijing
app:
     app_id: eb20****-e6ee-4f6d-a36f-5f6a5455****
```

Replace the parameter values in the preceding code with your actual values.

**Update a specified instance group and specify the deployment package version**

For example, you have an application with the ID `eb20dc8a-e6ee-4f6d-a36f-5f6a545****` in the China (Beijing) region and need to upgrade its application group with the ID `06923bb9-8c5f-4508-94d8-517b692f****` to deployment package version 1.2. The following code provides a sample configuration:

```java
env:
  region_id: cn-beijing
app:
  app_id: eb20dc8a-e6ee-4f6d-a36f-5f6a5455****
  package_version: 1.2
  group_id: 06923bb9-8c5f-4508-94d8-517b692f****
```

3. Create a YAML account file on your local machine, and configure the AccessKey ID and
AccessKey secret in the file. We recommend that you use the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of a RAM user with the **Application Management** permission to control application permissions and improve application security. To obtain the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret: RAM user: Click your profile picture in the upper-right corner of the page and select
**Personal Information**. You can find the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret in the
**AccessKey** area.
For an Alibaba Cloud account: a. In the top menu bar, click **Enterprise**. b. In the navigation pane on the left, select **Resource Management > Organization**
**Management**.
c. In the **Organization Structure** area, select the target organization. In the **Basic**
**Information** area on the right, click **Manage AccessKey**. In the dialog box that
appears, you can find the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. The following code shows a sample account file: anagement for ECS clusters

```
access_key_id: abc access_key_secret: 1234567890
```

**Note**

The parameter values in the example are for reference only. Replace them with your actual AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. The AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret in this configuration are used only to generate request signatures. They are not used for other purposes, such as network transfers.
4. In the local project folder (or the submodule folder for a Maven multi-module project),
execute the following command to package and deploy the application to EDAS.

```
mvn clean package toolkit:deploy -Daccess_key_file={Path of the account file}
```

Parameter descriptions: `toolkit:deploy` : A parameter of the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in that is used to deploy applications. If you configure this parameter, the application is deployed after it is successfully packaged. `access_key_file` : Specifies the path of the account file. You can also set the `-Djar_path` parameter to specify the file path of a deployment package to skip the packaging step and directly deploy an existing package. The path of the deployment package can be an absolute or relative path.

```
mvn toolkit:deploy -Daccess_key_file={Path of the account file} - Djar_path=target/demo.jar
```

**Important**

You can also configure the path of the account file in the `env` parameters. However, the path specified by the `-D` parameter takes precedence.

**Verify the result**

1. After you execute the application packaging and deployment commands, check the output
logs in the IDE terminal. A BUILD SUCCESS prompt is displayed, which indicates that the application is deployed successfully. If the output log contains ERROR information, use the log to troubleshoot the failure. Fix the error and redeploy the application.
2. Log on to the EDAS console. Then, check the change records and application details to
verify that the application is upgraded successfully. For more information, see Verify the result. anagement for ECS clusters

**Apsara Stack support**

The toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in is supported in Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition V3.8.0 and later. Before you use the plug-in, you must configure an EDAS Endpoint for it. Contact EDAS technical support to obtain the Endpoint.

**Use the CLI to quickly create an application**

Run the following script to quickly create an application in an ECS cluster. anagement for ECS clusters

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# The region where you want to deploy the application.
REGION="cn-beijing"
# The ID of the ECS instance.
ECS_ID="i-2z************b6"
# The ID of the VPC where the ECS instance resides.
VPC_ID="vpc-t**********c"
# The name of the microservice namespace. If the namespace does not exist, it is automa
tically created. NAMESPACE="myNamespace"
# The name of the cluster. The cluster is automatically created.
CLUSTER_NAME="myCluster"
# The name of the application.
APP_NAME="myApp"
# Step 1: Create a microservice namespace.
aliyun edas InsertOrUpdateRegion --RegionTag $REGION:$NAMESPACE --RegionName $NAMESPACE --region $REGION --endpoint "edas.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com" >> /dev/null
# Step 2: Create a cluster.
CLUSTER_ID=`aliyun edas InsertCluster --ClusterName $CLUSTER_NAME --ClusterType 2 --Net workMode 2 --VpcId $VPC_ID --logicalRegionId $REGION:$NAMESPACE --region $REGION --endp oint "edas.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com" | sed -E 's/.*"ClusterId":"([a-z0-9-]*)".*/\1/g'`
# Step 3: Import the ECS instance.
aliyun edas TransformClusterMember --InstanceIds $ECS_ID --TargetClusterId $CLUSTER_ID --Password Hello1234 >> /dev/null for i in `seq 300`
```

`do`

```bash
    OUT=`aliyun edas ListClusterMembers --ClusterId $CLUSTER_ID | grep EcuId` && break
    sleep 1
done ECU_ID=`echo $OUT | sed -E 's/.*"EcuId":"([a-z0-9-]*)".*/\1/g'`
# Step 4: Create an application.
APP_ID=`aliyun edas InsertApplication --ApplicationName $APP_NAME --BuildPackId 51 --Ec uInfo $ECU_ID --ClusterId $CLUSTER_ID --logicalRegionId $REGION:$NAMESPACE | sed -E 's/ .*"AppId":"([a-z0-9-]*)".*/\1/g'` printf "An application is created by CLI, App ID:"$APP_ID"\n"
```

**APP_ID** and **GROUP_ID** parameters with your actual values.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

ps. APP_ID="87a6*********************4d1"

The bucket must be publicly readable. OSS_BUCKET="eda*****mo"

aliyun oss cp -f $PACKAGE oss://$OSS_BUCKET/$PACKAGE >> /dev/null PKG_URL=`aliyun oss sign oss://$OSS_BUCKET/$PACKAGE|head -1`

# Step 3: Wait for the deployment to complete.
for i in `seq 300`
```

```
'.*"PipelineStatus":' | sed -E 's/.*"PipelineStatus":\s(.).*/\1/g'`

done
```
