#### Phased release in an ECS cluster

##### Release an application in phases in the

**EDAS console**

A phased release is recommended for applications that have many instances or a complex service architecture. This process updates the application on a small number of instances in each phase until all instances are updated. This topic describes how to use the Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) console to perform a phased release.

**Background information**

You can release an application in phases if it has multiple application instances. An Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster can contain instance groups, and each group can have multiple application instances. You can also perform a phased release based on instance groups.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region in the top menu bar, select a microservices
namespace, and then select ECS Clusters from the cluster type list. Then, click the name of the target application in the application list.
4. On the **Application Details** page, click **Deploy Application** in the upper-right corner.
5. On the **Select Deployment Mode** page, click **Start Deployment** in the upper-right
corner of the **Regular Release (Single-batch/Multi-batch)** section.
6. On the **Regular Release (Single-batch/Multi-batch)** page, set the deployment package
and related information for the new application version, configure the **Release Policy**, and then click **OK**. anagement for ECS clusters i. Set the deployment package and related information.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Enable application monitoring | If application monitoring is disabled, the monitoring and alerting, trace query, microservices query, service authentication, outlier removal, graceful undeployment, and canary release features are unavailable. |
| Deployment Method | The deployment method of the application. The deployment method is selected when the application is deployed for the first time. This method cannot be changed. For example, a JAR package is used when the application is deployed for the first time. You can specify only JAR as the deployment method when you update the application. Note If you set the Deployment Method parameter to Historical Versions, the application can be rolled back to an earlier version. For more information, see Use the EDAS console to roll back applications in ECS clusters. |
| File Uploading Method | The method that is used to upload the deployment package of the new version. You can upload a JAR or WAR package, or specify the URL of a JAR or WAR package. The type of the deployment package depends on the deployment package that is used when you deploy the application for the first time. If you select Upload JAR Package or Upload WAR Package, click Select File and upload the deployment package of the new version. If you select JAR Package Address or WAR Package Address, enter the URL of the deployment package into the field below. You must first upload the deployment package to a cloud service, such as Object Storage Service (OSS). |
| Version | The new version of the application. You can enter the version number or click Use Timestamp as Version Number. |
| Description | The description of the new version. |

anagement for ECS clusters ii. Configure the release policy.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Group | The target groups for the phased release. If the application has only one group, select All Groups from the list. The number in the parentheses after All Groups indicates the maximum number of application instances. The list also includes Default Group, which is the same as All Groups. If the application has multiple groups, select a target group from the list. Note If you select All Groups, the application is released to all groups in phases based on the Batches Per Group setting. |
| Batches Per Group | The number of release phases for the selected groups. The minimum number of instances per phase is 1. The default is 2 batches per group. Set this parameter as needed. |
| Batch Mode | The method used to proceed between release phases. Valid values:A utomatic and Manual. Automatic: The next phase starts automatically after the interval specified by Wait Time Before Next Batch. Manual: You must manually trigger the next phase. |
| Wait Time Before Next Batch | The interval between release phases, in minutes. Select an interval from the list as needed. |
| Java Environment | The Java environment for the new application version. Valid values include Open JDK 8, Open JDK 7, and Dragonwell 8. Select an environment as needed. |

iii. Click **OK**. After the phased release starts, you are automatically redirected to the **Change Details** page. In **Change Details**, you can track its progress and status. For more information, see the View Application Changes topic.

**Verify the results**

1. View change records.
i. On the application details page, click **Change Records** in the left-side navigation pane. anagement for ECS clusters ii. On the **Change Records** page, check whether the value in the **Change Status** column is **Success**. If the value is **Success**, the application is released. If the value is **Execute failed**, the application fails to be released. You can click **View** in the **Actions** column to view the change details and troubleshoot issues.
2. View application details.
i. On the application details page, click **Basic Information** in the left-side navigation pane. ii. Click the **Basic Information** tab. In the **Application Information** section of the **Basic**
**Information** tab, you can check whether **Deployment Package** shows the latest
deployment package. iii. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, check whether the **Running Status** column of each instance in the desired group is **Normal**.

##### Use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to

**perform a phased release of an application on an**

**ECS cluster**

Use the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to perform a phased release of a Spring Cloud, Dubbo, or HSF application deployed in EDAS. anagement for ECS clusters

**Background information**

The toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in is an open source tool that helps you establish a complete lifecycle framework and a basic toolset for your project. The toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in also supports application upgrades in EDAS Kubernetes clusters. For more information, see Use the Cloud Toolkit plug-in for single-batch release of an application (Kubernetes).

**Procedure**

1. Add the dependency for the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in to the pom.xml file in your local
project.

```xml
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>com.alibaba.cloud</groupId>
            <artifactId>toolkit-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>1.1.5</version>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

2. Create a configuration file named `.edas_config.yaml` in the root directory of the project
and set the deployment parameters in the file. A file whose name starts with a period ( `.` ) is the default configuration file for an integrated development environment (IDE). If you do not specify another configuration file, the plug-in uses the `.edas_config.yaml` file in the root directory by default. If you create a configuration file whose name does not start with a period ( `.` ), you can specify the file by setting the `-Dedas_config=xxx` parameter when you package the project. If a default configuration file exists and you also specify another configuration file using a parameter, the plug-in uses the file specified by the parameter.

**Note**

If the current project is a submodule of a Maven project, the default configuration file must be in the directory of the current project, not in the root directory of the parent Maven project. The following example shows the configuration for a typical upgrade scenario: For example, an application with the ID `eb20****-e6ee-4f6d-a36f-5f6a5455****` in the China (Hangzhou) region contains multiple application groups. You want to upgrade an

| 62fe****-d931-4446-a30a-f396a6da**** |   | . The re |
|---|---|---|
| d the wait time between batches is |   |   |

following is a sample configuration: anagement for ECS clusters

```
env:
  region_id: cn-hangzhou
app:
  app_id: e130****-75d7-471e-9e31-95145701****
  group_id: 62fe****-d931-4446-a30a-f396a6da****
  batch: 2
  batch_wait_time: 3
```

3. Create a YAML account file on your local machine and configure the AccessKey ID and
AccessKey secret in the file. Use the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of a Resource Access Management (RAM) user that has the **Application Management** permission. This practice improves security by controlling application permissions. You can view the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of a RAM user on the **Personal Information** page. The following code provides a sample account file:

```
access_key_id: abc access_key_secret: 1234567890
```

**Note**

The parameter values in the example are for reference only. Replace them with your actual AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. The AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret in this configuration are used only to generate request signatures and are not used for other purposes, such as network transfers.
4. In the local project directory, or the submodule directory for a multi-module Maven project,
run the following command to package and deploy the application to EDAS.

```
mvn clean package toolkit:deploy -Daccess_key_file={path_of_the_account_file}
```

Parameter description: `toolkit:deploy` : Deploys the application using the toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in. The application is deployed only after it is successfully packaged. `access_key_file` : The path of the account file. You can also set the `-Djar_path` parameter to specify the path of a deployment package. This skips the packaging step and directly deploys an existing package. The deployment package path can be an absolute path or a relative path.

```
mvn toolkit:deploy -Daccess_key_file={path_of_the_account_file} - Djar_path=target/demo.jar
```

**Important**

You can also configure the account file path in the `env` block. The `-D` parameter takes precedence over the configuration in the `env` block.

**Verify the result**

1. After you run the packaging and deployment command, view the output logs in the IDE
terminal. anagement for ECS clusters If the output logs show BUILD SUCCESS, the application is successfully deployed. If the output logs contain ERROR information, use the logs to identify the cause of the failure. Then, fix the error and deploy the application again.
2. Log on to the EDAS console. View the change records and application details to verify that
the application was successfully upgraded or deployed. For more information, see Verify the result.

**Apsara Stack support**

The toolkit-maven-plugin plug-in is available for Apsara Stack V3.8.0 and later. Before you use the plug-in, configure the EDAS Endpoint. Contact EDAS technical support to obtain the Endpoint.

#### Canary release

##### Release an application in canary mode in

**an ECS cluster in the EDAS console**

To update a Spring Cloud or Dubbo microservices application deployed in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster, you can perform a canary release to verify the new version on a small number of instances. If the verification is successful, you can then deploy the update to all instances.

**Prerequisites**

Before you perform a canary release, make sure that the application has at least two instance groups and that each group contains instances. For more information about how to create instance groups and add ECS instances to the groups, see Manage application instance groups in an ECS cluster using the console.

**Limits**

anagement for ECS clusters HSF applications: Canary release is not supported. Dubbo applications: No limits apply. Spring Cloud applications: Do not use canary release for applications that depend on features and configurations related to Deployment.Metadata.Name or Deployment.Metadata.Uid. Otherwise, these native features may not work as expected. Ingress applications: For ingress applications where traffic is forwarded directly from an SLB instance, the SLB traffic forwarding policy does not adhere to the canary release policy.

**Note**

To test a canary release, you can use a demo. Create a client application and a server application with multiple replicas. Perform a canary release for the server application. To access the service, attach an SLB instance to the client application.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region and a microservices namespace, and then click
the name of the target application.
4. In the upper-right corner of the application details page, click **Deploy Application**.
5. On the **Select Deployment Mode** page, in the top-right corner of the **Canary Release**
**(Phased)** area, click **Start Deployment**.
6. On the **Canary Release (Grayscale)** page, upload the deployment package for the new
application version, set the release policy and grayscale rules, and click **OK**. i. Upload the deployment package of the new application version. anagement for ECS clusters ii. In the **Release Policy** area, configure the policy parameters. The **Publish Policy Configuration** section on the right displays the phased release flow according to the configuration. The following table describes the release policy parameters.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Canary Group | The instance group for the canary release. |
| Batches per Group After Canary Release | After the canary release for the specified instance group is complete, the new version is deployed to instances in other groups in preset batches. If you select all groups, the new version is deployed to the instances in each group based on the selected number of batches. If the number of instances in a group is less than the selected number of batches, the new version is deployed to the instances in the group based on the number of instances. If you select a specific group, the new version is deployed to the instances in the specified group based on the selected number of batches. |
| Batch Type for Scale- out After Canary Release | This parameter must be configured if Batches Per Group After Grayscale is set to 2 or more, and has two modes:A utomatic and Manual. Automatic: Automatically performs a phased release based on the batch interval. This mode also requires you to set the Batch Wait Time. Wait Time Before Next Batch can be set to Do Not Wait or a value from 1 to 5 minutes. Manual: Manually trigger the publication of the next batch. |
| Java Environment | The runtime environment of the application. Select a runtime environment as needed. |

iii. Set canary rules. You can set canary rules via two methods: **Canary Release By Content** and **Canary**
**Release By Ratio**.
anagement for ECS clusters
**Content-based Grayscale**: Click **Add Policy**. Then, click **Create Traffic Rule** to set
an ingress traffic rule.

**Note**

You can create multiple ingress traffic rules. The following table describes the parameters for Canary Release by Content.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Protocol Type | Includes Spring Cloud and Dubbo. Select an option based on your application's requirements. Spring Cloud: You need to set the path. Dubbo: You must select a Service and a Method. |
| Condition Pattern | Includes Meet All Conditions and Meet Any Condition. |
| Conditions | The conditions for the Spring Cloud and Dubbo protocols are different. The available methods are Cookie, Header, and Parameter. Select a method based on your actual requirements. Spring Cloud: Set the method to Cookie, Header, or Parameter based on your actual needs. Dubbo: Set the Parameter and the Parameter Value Expression based on your application. |

anagement for ECS clusters
**Grayscale By Ratio**: Forwards traffic to the current grayscale group based on the
specified **Traffic Ratio** . After the canary release starts, the new application version is deployed to the specified instance group. On the **Basic Information** page, the message A change process is ongoing for this application. The application is in Executing state appears. You can click
**View Details** to open the **Change Details** page and view the deployment progress and
status. Stop the change: The change has been stopped. The application is in a canary release. You must roll back the application before performing other operations.
7. Check whether the canary traffic is distributed as expected. For more information, see
Monitor canary traffic.
8. After the grayscale traffic is verified, on the **Change Details** page, click **Start Next Batch**
to continue the phased release. If you find an issue with the new application version during the verification process, you can click the **Stop Change** button in the upper-right corner of the **Change Details** page. After the change is stopped, the **Basic Information** page displays the following message: The application is in the canary release state and this change has been stopped. Roll back the application before you perform other operations.

**Verify the result**

After the phased release, on the **Basic Information** page, check that the **Deployment**
**Package** is the new application version. On the **Instance Deployment Information** page,
check that the **Running Status** of the application instance is **Normal**.

##### Release an application in an ECS cluster in

**canary mode using an API**

This topic describes how to use the Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) SDK for Java to release an application in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster in canary mode using an API.

**Prerequisites**

Before you release an application in an ECS cluster in canary mode, complete the following prerequisites: The Java SDK for EDAS is installed. For more information, see the **EDAS Developer Guide**
**> SDK Reference**.
Obtain the ID of the region where you want to create the ECS cluster. A microservices namespace has been created. For more information, see Manage microservices namespaces using APIs. If a namespace already exists, you can call the ListUserDefineRegion operation to query the list of user-defined namespaces and obtain the RegionId of the target namespace. An application has been created in the ECS cluster. For more information, see Create an application using an API (ECS). If an application already exists, you can call the ListApplication operation to query the list of applications and obtain the **APPId** of the target application. For example, the application ID is 6bbc57a2-a017-4bec-b521-49a15bd3****. Upload the application deployment package (JAR or WAR) to a destination. This topic uses an Object Storage Service (OSS) path as an example: https:doc***.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyunc s.com/sc-****-D-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar. anagement for ECS clusters Call the ListDeployGroup operation to query the list of application instance groups and obtain the **GroupId** of the target group. For example, the group ID is 941be68c-4aac-48a1- 88fe-c9ad1502****. To create a High-Speed Service Framework (HSF) application, call the **EDAS Developer**
**Guide > ListBuildPack** operation to query the list of container versions and obtain the
container version parameter (`ConfigId`). For example, the value can be 57.

#### Roll back applications

##### Roll back applications in ECS clusters

**using the console**

If an error occurs during an application upgrade, or if the application does not function correctly after an upgrade, you can roll back the application. After you resolve the issue, you can upgrade the application again.

**Background information**

Rollback during an upgrade: If you find an error during a single-batch, phased, or canary release, you can stop the process and roll back the application. Rollback after an upgrade: If an application does not function correctly after a single-batch, phased, or canary release is complete, you can roll back the application by deploying a historical version.

**Roll back during an upgrade**

If you find an error while upgrading an application, you can stop the process and roll it back. You can upgrade applications using single-batch release, phased release, or canary release. The following sections describe how to roll back an application during each type of upgrade.

**Roll back during a single-batch release**

For more information about how to perform a single-batch release, see Use the console to upgrade an application (ECS cluster). After the single-batch release starts, the **Change Details** page is displayed. To stop the change, click **Stop Change** in the upper-right corner of the **Change Details** page.

**Roll back during a phased release**

For more information about how to perform a phased release, see Use the console to release an application in phases. After the phased release starts, the **Change Details** page appears. The rollback procedure depends on the phased release mode. Roll back during an automatic phased release In this scenario, you do not need to manually trigger the release of the next batch because it is automatically released after a specified interval. You can verify the new version of the application during this interval. If you find a problem, you can stop the upgrade and roll back the application. To do this, click **Stop Change** in the upper-right corner of the
**Change Details** page.
Roll back during a manual phased release In this scenario, you must manually release the next batch. Before doing so, you can verify the new version of the application. If you find an issue, click **Stop Change** in the upperright corner of the **Change Details** page. anagement for ECS clusters

**Roll back during a canary release**

For more information about how to perform a canary release, see Use the console for a canary release (ECS cluster). After the canary release starts, the **Change Details** page appears. During a canary release, you must manually trigger subsequent phased releases. If you find a problem or an error after verifying the canary release version, click **Stop Change** in the upper-right corner of the
**Change Details** page.

**Roll back after an upgrade**

If an application upgrade is complete but the new version does not function as expected, you can roll back the application by deploying a historical version.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region and a **Microservices Namespace** from the top
of the page, select **ECS Clusters** from the cluster type list, and then click the name of your target application in the application list.
4. In the upper-right corner of the **Basic Information** page, click **Roll Back Application**.
5. In the **Roll Back Application** dialog box, select a previous version from the **Deployment**
**Package Version** drop-down list, set the parameters, and click **Roll Back Application**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

anagement for ECS clusters

| Group | The group of the application to be rolled back. If the current application has only one group, select All Groups from the drop-down list. The maximum number of instances for the current application is displayed in parentheses after the group name. The drop-down list also includes Default Group, which is the same as All Groups. If the current application has multiple groups, select a group as needed. Note If you select All Groups, the rollback is performed based on the Batches Per Group settings. |
|---|---|
| Batches Per Group | The number of batches in the group. The minimum number of instances in a single batch is 1. The default number of instances in a single batch is 2. Specify this parameter as needed. |
| Batch Mode | The method used to release the next batch. Valid values:A utomatic and Manual. Automatic: The next batch is automatically released based on theW ait Time Before Next Batch parameter. Manual: The next batch is manually released. |
| Wait Time Before Next Batch | The interval between the release of two batches. The unit is minutes. Select an interval from the drop-down list as needed. |

**Verify the results**

1. View the change records.
i. On the application details page, click **Change Records** in the left navigation pane. ii. On the **Change Records** page, check the **Change Status** column to verify that the rollback status is **Executed Successfully**. A status of **Executed Successfully** indicates that the application has been rolled back. The **Execution Failed** status indicates a failed rollback. In the **Actions** column, click
**View** to check the change details and troubleshoot the failure.
2. View the application details.
i. On the application details page, click **Basic Information** in the left navigation pane. ii. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Basic Information** tab. In the **Application**
**Information** section of the **Basic Information** tab, check that the **Deployment**
**Package** is a historical package.
iii. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, check that the **Running Status** of each instance in the target group is **Normal**.

##### Use an API to roll back an application in an

**ECS cluster to a historical version**

anagement for ECS clusters This topic describes how to roll back an application in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster to a target historical version by calling an API with the Java software development kit (SDK) for Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS).

**Prerequisites**

Before you roll back an application to a target historical version, complete the following prerequisites: Install the Java SDK for EDAS. For more information, see **EDAS Developer Guide > SDK**
**Reference**.
Determine the region where the ECS cluster is located. The application has been upgraded. You can use one of the following methods: Use an API to deploy an application in a single batch in an ECS cluster Use an API to deploy an application in phases in an ECS cluster Use an API for canary release (ECS cluster) Call the **EDAS Developer Guide > ListHistoryDeployVersion** operation to query the historical versions of the application and obtain the **PackageVersion** of the target version. For example, 20210417.154931. Call the **EDAS Developer Guide > ListDeployGroup** operation to query the application instance groups and obtain the **GroupId** of the target application instance group. For example, 941be68c-4aac-48a1-88fe-c9ad1502****.

**Roll back an application to a target historical version**

The following sample code shows how to roll back an application in an EDAS ECS cluster to a target historical version.

```java
import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ServerException; import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile; import com.aliyuncs.edas.model.v20170801.RollbackApplicationRequest; import com.aliyuncs.edas.model.v20170801.RollbackApplicationResponse; public class RollbackApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args)  {
        // An AccessKey pair of an Alibaba Cloud account has permissions on all API ope
rations. Using an AccessKey pair is a high-risk operation. We recommend that you create and use a Resource Access Management (RAM) user for API calls and routine O&M. To creat e a RAM user, log on to the RAM console.
```

### Application monitoring

Application monitoring accurately displays an application's real-time traffic and historical data. Use this information to monitor application health and to quickly locate and resolve issues. EDAS provides monitoring features through Application Real-Time Monitoring Service (ARMS). These features include application overviews, application details, and interface calls.

**Monitoring data types**

| Configuration | Description |
|---|---|
| Application Overview | Shows the overall status of services that the application provides and calls. |
| My Entry Points | Shows the application's entry points. An entry point is a frontend request, usually based on the HTTP protocol. |
| Provided RPC Services | Shows when the application acts as a server to provide RPC services. This includes HSF and other custom types. |
| RPC Call Sources | Shows when clients call the application, which acts as a server. |
| RPC Call Dependencies | Shows when the application acts as a client to call RPC services. This includes HSF and other custom types. |
| Database Access | Shows when the application acts as a client to access a database. |
| Message Types | Shows when the application produces and consumes messages. |

**Application monitoring FAQ**

1. . Why does the application monitoring data page appear gray and fail to open?**
Reason: This issue occurs because you have not purchased a certificate. The ARMS page uses a self-signed or invalid certificate for HTTPS, which is blocked by the browser. Solution: To resolve this issue, open the blocked ARMS page in a new browser tab. Then, open the page again in EDAS.
2. . Why is there no monitoring data after an application upgrade?**
Reason: This issue occurs after an upgrade because the EDAS monitoring solution changed in version 3.9.0. You must manually restart the application to enable monitoring. Solution: Hot-upgraded applications must be restarted before you can view infrastructure monitoring and service monitoring data. If you cannot restart the application, remotely connect to the ECS instance and perform the following steps:
1. Reinstall EDAS Agent. For more information, see Install EDAS Agent for an ECS instance.
2. Switch to the admin user and run the `edas refresh-apm` command.
anagement for ECS clusters

#### Application monitoring overview

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) is integrated with Application Real-Time Monitoring Service (ARMS). This lets you monitor the health status and key metrics of Java applications deployed in EDAS within Elastic Compute Service (ECS) environments. You can also configure alert rules for monitoring metrics to promptly detect and resolve abnormal conditions or faults. This ensures the health and availability of your applications.

**Application monitoring**

The application monitoring feature provides three levels of monitoring for applications in ECS environments: application overview, application details, and interface call.

**Note**

Application overview, application details, and interface call are provided by ARMS as service components in EDAS. ARMS does not charge for these features. If you want to use the full application monitoring capabilities of ARMS, go to the
**Advanced Monitoring** page and click **Enable Advanced Application**
**Monitoring** to connect the current application to ARMS. After you enable advanced
monitoring, the application is billed according to the billing rules of ARMS.

| Monitoring granularity | Description | References |
|---|---|---|
| Application Overview | Displays the health status and key metrics of the application. This includes an overview, related events, provided services, dependent services, and system information, such as CPU, memory, and load. | For more information, see the Application Overview section. |
| Application Details | Displays an overview and core metrics for the application and its instances, such as data for Java Virtual Machine (JVM), host, SQL calls, NoSQL calls, errors, upstream and downstream applications, and interfaces. | For more information, see the following documents: JVM monitoring Host monitoring |
| Interface Call | Displays an overview and core metrics at the interface level, such as data for SQL calls, NoSQL calls, errors, upstream and downstream links, and interfaces. | For more information, see the Interface call section. |

**Alerting**

You can create alert rules for monitoring metrics. If an alert rule is triggered, the system sends a notification to an alert contact group using your specified notification methods. This allows the contacts to take prompt action. References: Manage contacts anagement for ECS clusters Create and manage contact groups Create alerts Manage alerts

#### Application overview

On the **Application Overview** page, you can view key health metrics for an application. These metrics include overall indicators such as total requests and average response time, metrics for provided and dependent services, and system information such as CPU and memory usage.

**Access the feature**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Application Monitoring > Application**
**Overview**.

**Overview analysis**

The **Overview Analysis** tab displays the following key metrics: Total requests, average response time, real-time instance count, number of full garbage collection (GC) events, and number of slow SQL statements for a selected time range, along with their day-over-day and week-over-week change rates. Services provided by the application: Time series curves for the number of requests and average response time. Application dependencies: Time series curves for the number of requests, average response time, and application instance count, along with HTTP status code statistics. System information: Time series curves for CPU, MEM, and Load.

**Topology tab**

anagement for ECS clusters On the **Topology** tab, you can view the upstream and downstream components of your application and the call relationship between the components and the application in the topology. The topology helps you identify the bottlenecks of your application.

**Copy a view**

You can use the Copy View feature to create a custom topology.
1. Click **Copy View**. In the dialog box that appears, configure the **View Name** parameter and
specify whether to set the view as the default view.
2. Click **Edit Topology** and perform the following operations to adjust the topology:
i. Right-click a node to view the upstream nodes, downstream nodes, and details of the node, copy the node information, or remove the node. ii. Double-click a node to view its downstream nodes. iii. Move the pointer over a node or a dot on a line between nodes to view the following information: a. Service name b. QPS: the number of queries per second c. RT: the response time in milliseconds d. ERROR: the number of failed queries per second
3. Click **OK**.

**Edit or delete a view**

You can edit or delete a custom topology.
1. Select a view from the drop-down list on the right of **Copy View** and click **Edit**.
2. In the dialog box that appears, change the view name.
3. Click **Edit Topology** to modify the view, and then click **OK**.
4. If the current topology is no longer needed, click **Delete** in the upper-right corner to delete
it.

#### Application Details

The EDAS application details page integrates various ARMS monitoring capabilities. This page helps you quickly identify faulty and slow interfaces, reproduce call parameters, detect memory leaks, and discover system bottlenecks, which significantly improves the efficiency of diagnosing online issues.

**Feature Entry**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Application Monitoring > Application Details**.

**Overview: Automatically Discover and Monitor Interfaces**

EDAS automatically discovers and monitors common web and RPC frameworks in your application code. It also automatically collects metrics such as call volume, response time, and error count for the corresponding interfaces. anagement for ECS clusters

**JVM Monitoring**

The **JVM Monitoring** tab displays the instantaneous GC count and time, details for heap memory and metaspace, non-heap memory, direct buffer, and time series curves for the JVM thread count.

**Pooling Monitoring**

The **Pooling Monitoring** tab displays various metrics for the thread pools used by the application, including core thread count, current thread count, maximum thread count, active thread count, and queue size.

**Host Monitoring**

The **Host Monitoring** tab displays time series curves for CPU, memory, disk, load, network traffic, and network packets.

**SQL Call Analysis**

The **SQL Call Analysis** tab displays a list of database call requests initiated by the selected interface. On this tab, you can view the number of database calls and call time for the selected interface to determine which database call is slow.

**NoSQL Call Analysis**

The **NoSQL Call Analysis** tab displays a list of NoSQL requests initiated per minute by the selected interface. On this tab, you can identify which NoSQL request causes an interface to be slow. You can also click an interface snapshot within a NoSQL request to view the complete code path of its execution logic.

**Exception Analysis**

The **Exception Analysis** tab displays a stacked column chart of application exceptions and an exception list for a specified time range.

**Error Analysis**

The **Error Analysis** tab displays the application's error count and HTTP status code statistics. You can click a TraceID to view its related call chain information on a new page.

**Upstream Applications**

The **Upstream Applications** tab displays time series curves for the response time, request count, and error count of upstream applications for a specified time range.

**Interface Snapshot**

On the **Interface Snapshot** tab, you can view the interface name, its associated application, and information such as its time consumption status and TraceID.

#### Interface calls

The Interface Calls feature monitors your application's interface calls. You can view details such as SQL analysis, NoSQL call analysis, error analysis, upstream and downstream services, and interface snapshots.

**Supported frameworks**

This feature can automatically detect and monitor the APIs provided in the following web frameworks and remote procedure call (RPC) frameworks: Tomcat 7+ anagement for ECS clusters Jetty 8+ Resin 3.0+ Undertow 1.3+ WebLogic 11.0+ SpringBoot 1.3.0+ HSF 2.0+ Dubbo 2.5+ SOFABoot 3.2.0+

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Application Monitoring > Interface Call**.

**View overview information**

The **Overview** tab on the **Interface Calls** page lists all APIs that the application monitoring agent automatically discovers. You can sort the list by response time, number of requests, or number of errors. Select an API to view its detailed call topology, timing curves for requests, response time, and errors, and HTTP status code statistics on the **Overview** tab.

**SQL call analysis**

The **SQL Call Analysis** tab displays a list of database calls initiated by the selected API. On this tab, you can view the number of database calls and the call time for the selected API. This helps you identify which database call is too slow.

**NoSQL call analysis**

The **NoSQL Call Analysis** tab displays a list of NoSQL requests initiated per minute by the selected API. On this tab, you can identify which NoSQL request is slowing down an API. You can also click an interface snapshot of a NoSQL request to view its complete code trace.

**Error analysis**

The **Error Analysis** tab displays statistics on application errors and HTTP status codes. You can also click a TraceId to view the corresponding call trace on a new page.

**Upstream and downstream service calls**

The **Upstream** and **Downstream** tabs list the upstream services that call the application and the downstream services that the application calls, respectively. You can view their call performance metrics, such as the number of requests, response time, and number of errors. On the **Upstream** and **Downstream** tabs, you can perform the following operations: At the top of the tab, click **Collapse/Expand All** to collapse or expand all APIs. In the search box at the top of the tab, enter a keyword from an application or API (Span) name and click the search icon to find matching APIs. Click an API or the arrow icon at the end of its row to expand or collapse its performance metrics. anagement for ECS clusters

**Interface snapshots**

After you select an API, you can view the details for each of its individual calls. These details include the creation time, API name, parent application, time consumed, status, and TraceId.

#### Alerting

##### Manage contacts

When an alert rule is triggered, notifications are sent to the contact group that you specified. Before you create a contact group, you must create contacts. When you create a contact, you can specify a mobile phone number and an email address on which the contact can receive notifications. You can also provide the webhook URL of a DingTalk chatbot that can be used to automatically send alert notifications.

**Prerequisites**

To add a DingTalk robot as a contact, you must first obtain its webhook URL. For more information, see Set up DingTalk robot alerts.

**Create a contact**

anagement for ECS clusters
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, click the name of the target application.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Alert Management > Contact Management**.
5. On the **Contact Management** page, click **Contacts**. On the **Contacts** tab, click **Create**

##### Create an alert

You can create alerts to define rules for specific monitored objects. When a rule is triggered, the system sends an alert notification to a contact group using your specified method, prompting you to take the necessary action to resolve the issue.

**Prerequisites**

Create and manage a contact group. Only contact groups can receive alert notifications.

**Background information**

Default alert conditions: anagement for ECS clusters To prevent excessive notifications, the system sends only one message for a recurring alert within a 24-hour period. If an alert is not triggered again within 5 minutes, a recovery notification is sent to indicate that the metric has returned to normal. After the recovery notification is sent, the alert status is reset. If the alert is triggered again, it is treated as a new alert. An alert control displays data from a dataset. When you create an alert control, a corresponding dataset is created to store the underlying data.

**Note**

An alert rule takes about 10 minutes to take effect. There is a 1- to 3-minute delay in alert evaluation.

**Create an alert**

To create an alert based on a period-over-period comparison of Java Virtual Machine (JVM) garbage collection (GC) times for an application monitoring job, follow these steps:
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS Cluster**. On the **Applications** page,
click the name of the application for which you want to create a contact group.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Alert Management > Alert Policy**
**Management**.
5. In the upper-right corner of the **Alert Rules And History** page, click **Create Alert**.
6. In the **Create Alert** dialog box, configure the parameters and click **Save**.
Alert parameters:

| Field | Description | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Alert Name | The name of the alert. | None. |
| Application Group | The target application group. | Select an application group from the drop-down list. |
| Type | The type of the alert metric. | For application monitoring, the options are JVM Monitoring, Abnormal Interface Calls, MQ Metrics, Application Call Type Statistics, Host Monitoring, Application Call Statistics, and Database Metrics. |
| Dimension | The dimension of the alert metric. The options are None, =, and Traverse. | If you select None, the alert content shows the sum of all values for the dimension. The = operator requires you to manually enter a specific value. If you select Traverse, the alert content shows the dimension value that triggered the alert. |

anagement for ECS clusters

| Alert Rules And History | You can select All Of The Following Rules Are Met or Any Of The Following Rules Is Met. | None. |
|---|---|---|
| Last N Minutes | The time range for querying data to check against the trigger condition. | The value of N can be an integer from 3 to 3,600. The unit is minutes. |
| Notification Method | The method used to send alert notifications. The options are Email, Text Message, DingTalk Robot, and Webhook. | You can select multiple methods. For more information about how to configure DingTalk Robot alerts, see Set up DingTalk Robot alerts. |
| Notification Recipient | The contact group that receives alert notifications. | Add contact groups from the list on the left to the list on the right. |
| Alert Cool- down Period Switch | You can enable or disable this feature. It is enabled by default. | Enabled: If an alert is continuously triggered, a second notification is sent 24 hours after the first. When the metric returns to normal, you receive a recovery notification and the alert is cleared. If the alert is triggered again, a new notification is sent. Disabled: If an alert is continuously triggered, a notification is sent every minute. |
| Alert Data Revision Policy | The revision policy for alert data. | For more information, see Meanings of common complex fields. |
| Alert Level | The severity level of the alert. The options are Warning, Error, and Critical. | None. |
| Effective Period | The period during which the alert rule is active. | None. |
| Notification Time | The time range during which alert notifications are sent. Notifications are not sent outside this time range, but alert events are still recorded. | None. |
| Notification Content | The content of the alert notification, which you can customize. | You can edit the default template. The template supports only the `$AlertName`, `$Filter`, `$AlertTime`, and `$AlertContent` variables. You can customize the rest of the content. |

anagement for ECS clusters

**Meanings of common complex fields**

**Period-over-period comparisons**

Percentage increase or decrease from the previous period: β is the metric value for the last N minutes (average, sum, maximum, or minimum), and α is the metric value for the period from 2N minutes ago to N minutes ago. The comparison is between β and α. α β Now 2N N i i Percentage increase or decrease from the same period in the last hour: β is the metric value for the last N minutes (average, sum, maximum, or minimum), and α is the metric value for the same N-minute period of the previous hour. The comparison is between β and α. α β N minutes + 1 hour Now N h i Percentage increase or decrease from the same period on the previous day: β is the metric value for the last N minutes (average, sum, maximum, or minimum), and α is the metric value for the same N-minute period on the previous day. The comparison is between β and α. α β N minutes + 1 day Now N d i

**Alert data revision policy**

The alert data revision policy can be set to Fill with 0, Fill with 1, or Fill with Null (default). This feature is used to handle abnormal data, such as missing data, compound indicators, and period-over-period comparisons. Fill with 0: Replaces a null value with 0. Fill with 1: Replaces a null value with 1. Fill with Null: Retains the null value. A null value does not trigger an alert. Scenarios: Scenario 1: No data A user wants to monitor page views using alerts. The user creates a Browser Monitoring alert and sets the rule to trigger an alert if the total number of page views is less than or equal to 10 in the last 5 minutes (N=5). If the page is not accessed, no data is reported and no alert is sent. To resolve this issue, you can set the alert data revision policy to Fill with 0. This policy treats the absence of data as 0, which meets the alert rule and triggers an alert. Scenario 2: Abnormal compound indicator anagement for ECS clusters A user wants to use the alert feature to monitor the real-time unit price of a product. The user creates a custom monitoring alert, setting the dataset for variable 'a' to the current total price and for variable 'b' to the current total number of products. The alert rule is set to trigger if the minimum value of the compound indicator "(current total price) or (current total number of products)" is less than or equal to 10 for three consecutive data points (N=3). If the current total number of products is 0, a value for the compound indicator " (current total price) or (current total number of products)" is not generated, and an alert is not sent. To resolve this issue, you can select the "fill with zero" option for the alert data revision policy. This policy sets the value of the compound indicator to 0 if a value does not exist. Because this value now meets the alert rule, an alert is sent. Scenario 3: Abnormal period-over-period comparison A user wants to monitor the user CPU usage of a node. The user creates an application monitoring alert and sets the rule to trigger an alert if the average user CPU usage drops by 100% compared with the previous period in the last 3 minutes (N=3). If the user's CPU fails and does not report data in the last N minutes, the value of α cannot be obtained and the period-over-period result is null. As a result, no alert is sent. To resolve this issue, you can set the alert data revision policy to Fill with 1. This policy treats the period-over-period result as a 100% decrease, which meets the alert rule and triggers an alert.

### Application O&M

anagement for ECS clusters

#### Manage the lifecycle of applications in

**ECS clusters**

This topic describes how to use Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) to create, deploy, update, start, stop, reset, restart, and delete applications in Elastic Compute Service (ECS) clusters.

**Create and deploy an application**

You can develop Java applications based on frameworks such as Dubbo, Spring Cloud, and High-Speed Service Framework (HSF). Then, you can deploy the application packages (JAR and WAR packages) to ECS clusters in EDAS using the console, APIs, or tool plug-ins. For more information, see Overview of application creation and deployment (ECS).

**Upgrade and roll back an application**

After you create and deploy an application in EDAS, you can continuously upgrade it as your business grows. You can perform canary releases, phased releases, or single-batch releases for your application based on your upgrade needs. You can perform these releases using the console, APIs, or tool plug-ins. If you find an issue in a new version after an upgrade, you can roll back the application to a specific previous version. For more information, see Overview of application upgrades and rollbacks (ECS).

**Start and stop an application**

You can stop a running application as needed. After an application is stopped, billing and metering for its instances are paused. An application must have at least one instance before you can start or stop it. When you start or stop an application, all its instances are started or stopped. However, if an application has multiple instances, you can start or stop a single instance without affecting the others.

**Important**

If a stopped application depends on other services, such as Server Load Balancer (SLB) or Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), those services are still billed.

**Start or stop an application**

On the application's **Basic Information** page, click **Stop Application** or **Start**
**Application** in the upper-right corner.

**Start or stop an application instance**

On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, click **Enable** or **Stop** in the **Actions** column to start or stop an instance. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, click **Process Instances In Batch**. In the **Process Instances In Batch** dialog box, you can select multiple application instances to start or stop.

**Delete an application**

On the application's **Basic Information** page, click **Delete Application** in the upper-right corner.

**Reset an application**

anagement for ECS clusters On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, click **Reset** in the **Actions** column for an application instance to reconfigure its runtime environment. The version of the runtime environment remains unchanged after the reset.

**Restart an application**

To restart a running application instance, click **Restart** in the **Actions** column on the
**Instance Deployment Information** tab. This action stops the instance and then restarts it.

#### Server loading balancing

##### Overview

If you use Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) to host applications in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) environment, you can attach a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance to an application. The SLB instance distributes traffic to multiple backend application instances (ECS instances) based on forwarding rules. This increases service capacity and improves application availability. Operations that you perform on the SLB instance in the EDAS console are synchronized with the SLB console in real time. You do not need to perform the same operations in both the EDAS and SLB consoles.

**How to select a listener protocol**

A Server Load Balancer (SLB) listener determines how requests are forwarded to backend servers. When applications deployed in EDAS use SLB, you must select a listener protocol. For more information about listeners, see **Server Load Balancer User Guide**. Applications in ECS clusters support Layer 4 (TCP) and Layer 7 (HTTP) listeners. Select a listener protocol based on your application scenario.
**TCP**: Suitable for scenarios that require high reliability and data accuracy, even if transfer
speeds are relatively slow. Examples include file transfers, sending or receiving emails, and remote logons.
**HTTP**: Suitable for applications that need to identify data content, such as web applications
and small mobile games.

**How to select a load balancing method for an application**

Different load balancing methods are available for different scenarios.

| Scenario | References |
|---|---|
| Using a dedicated SLB instance for a single application. | Use a dedicated SLB instance for an application |
| Using URLs to distribute traffic among different instance groups of a single application. | Use URLs to forward traffic to application instance groups |
| Using ports to distribute traffic when multiple applications share an SLB instance. | Use ports to forward traffic (shared SLB instance) |

anagement for ECS clusters

| Using a domain name or URL to distribute traffic when multiple applications share an SLB instance. | Use a domain name or URL to forward traffic (shared SLB instance) |
|---|---|

**Balancer User Guide**.

To do this, attach an SLB instance to the application. This topic uses an Internet-facing SLB instance as an example. The procedure for an internalfacing SLB instance is the same. However, during verification, make sure to select the correct network environment.

of **SLB (Internet)**.

If an SLB instance is already configured, its IP address and port are displayed. Click
**Modify** to change the SLB instance information, or click **Detach** to detach the current
SLB instance.
5. In the **Add Binding for SLB and Application** wizard, configure the SLB instance.

Enter the correct _ health check path for your application. For more information, see Configure A Health Check > Server Load Balancer User Guide. |

##### Use URLs to distribute traffic to

**application instance groups**

After you attach a Server Load Balancer (SLB) instance to an application in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) cluster, you can configure URL-based forwarding policies for different application instance groups. The SLB instance forwards requests from different paths to the corresponding application instance groups based on the configured policies. This topic describes how to use URL-based forwarding policies to distribute traffic among different instance groups within an application.

**Prerequisites**

An SLB instance is created. For more information, see the **Server Load Balancer User**
**Guide > Create an Instance** section.
Different instance groups are created for the application. For more information, see Create a group. The SLB instance is attached to the application instances. For more information, see Application-exclusive SLB instance.

**Background information**

In an ECS cluster, you can create multiple application instance groups and deploy different deployment package versions to them. After you attach an SLB instance to the application, one of the following situations can occur: If no forwarding policies are configured for the application instance groups, traffic is randomly forwarded to the application instances in each group. If forwarding policies are configured for the application instance groups, requests from different paths are forwarded to the corresponding application instance groups. For example, in a flash sale scenario, the URL for querying product information in an ordering system (o.domain.com/orders/queryitem) is accessed more frequently than the URLs for other services. You can deploy the product information query service to a dedicated flash sale group and deploy other services to the default group. Then, you can configure URL-based forwarding policies for the SLB instance to forward product information query requests to the flash sale group and all other requests to the default group. anagement for ECS clusters

**Configure vServer groups and forwarding policies for**

**application groups**

You can configure vServer groups and forwarding policies for the attached SLB instance for the two groups in the example scenario.

**Note**

The procedure is similar for both groups. However, you cannot use the same vServer group for both application groups.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab.
5. On the **Instance Deployment Information** tab, to the right of the first group (the default
group), click **Group Settings** and select **Internet-facing SLB Information** from the drop-down list.
6. In the **Group Settings** dialog box, select a vServer group, set the forwarding rule, and
click **Next**. You can configure a vServer group and a URL-based forwarding policy for an application group in one of the following two ways: If you want to use a vServer group that has already been created for the selected SLB instance, perform the following operations: a. Select **Existing vServer Group**, and then select an existing vServer group.

**Important**

A vServer group can be attached to only one application or application group. b. Set a forwarding policy. If you want to use the forwarding rules that are already configured for this vServer group, select **Modify the forwarding policy of the current VServer group** and select the existing forwarding rules. If the vServer group does not have a forwarding rule or you want to add a new one, select **Add Forwarding Policy**, and then enter the domain name and path in the text box next to **Forwarding Rule**. If a vServer group is not configured for the selected SLB instance or you want to create a new vServer group for the current application, perform the following operations: anagement for ECS clusters a. Select **Create vServer Group**, and enter a **vServer Group Name**. b. Select **Add Forwarding Policy**, and in the text box next to **Forwarding Rule**, enter the domain name and path.

#### Application scale-out and scale-in

##### Manually scale out and scale in an

**application**

When service traffic is high and the application load is excessive, you can add ECS instances to scale out an application and distribute the load. When service traffic is low and the load on instances is light, you can remove instances to scale in the application and reduce costs.

**Scale out an application**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. On the **Basic Information** page, in the upper-right corner of the **Instance Deployment**
**Information** tab, click **Application Scale-out**.
5. In the **Add Instance** dialog box, on the **Scale-out Method** tab, select the **Target Group**
and the ECS instances to add, and then click **Scale-out**. anagement for ECS clusters

**Note**

The runtime state of an added instance is determined by the runtime state of the application. If the application is running, the added instance automatically deploys and starts the application. If the application is stopped, the added instance deploys the application but does not start it. The application on the instance remains in a stopped state.

**Scale in an application**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. On the **Basic Information** page, click the **Instance Deployment Information** tab.
5. On the **Instance Deployment Information** page, take the instance offline.
If the instance is in the **Running** state, click **Stop** and then click **Delete**. If the instance is **Stopped**, click **Delete**.

##### Perform auto scaling on applications in

**ECS clusters**

Auto Scaling is a key operations and maintenance (O&M) capability for managing distributed applications. It monitors the status of each application instance and dynamically scales the application out or in. This ensures service quality and improves application availability.

**Overview of Auto Scaling**

Applications in industries such as the Internet and gaming are prone to sudden traffic bursts during promotional activities. The imbalance between Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) and resource costs can cause issues such as system response latency and system breakdowns. EDAS uses the same traffic management technology that Alibaba uses for the Double 11 shopping festival. This provides second-level automatic elastic scaling to reduce instance retention costs and ensure your SLA is met. Auto Scaling is widely used in industries such as the Internet, gaming, and social networking. Auto Scaling applies to applications created in **ECS Clusters**. In a single-instance environment, Auto Scaling ensures that one instance is always running. For environments with fluctuating traffic, you can specify a range for the number of running instances. EDAS then adds or removes instances based on the configured load rules. Auto Scaling determines whether to scale out or scale in based on the following metrics of an application instance:
**CPU**: The percentage of CPU utilization.
**RT**: The time taken to respond to a request, measured in milliseconds (ms).
**Load**: A positive integer that represents the load on the application instance.
**mem**: The memory usage percentage.

**Configure automatic elastic scaling**

anagement for ECS clusters Auto Scaling includes automatic scale-out and scale-in operations. You can configure separate rules for each. The following procedure describes how to configure a scale-out rule.

**Note**

When you configure both scale-in and scale-out rules, the metric values for the scale-in rules must not be greater than those for the scale-out rules. Otherwise, an error message appears when you click **Save**. If you use elastic resources, instances from these resources are released first during a scale-in operation.
1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. In the left navigation pane on the application details page, click **Auto Scaling**.
5. In the upper-right corner of the **Scale-out Rule** area, turn on the switch to enable the rule.
6. Configure the scale-out rule parameters, and in the lower-left corner of the **Auto Scaling**
page, click **Save**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Trigger Metric | Set the thresholds for the Response Time (RT), Load, CPU, and mem metrics. A scale-out is triggered when a threshold is exceeded. |
| Trigger Condition | Any Metric: A scale-out is triggered if any of the specified metrics is triggered. All Metrics: A scale-out is triggered only if all of the specified metrics are triggered. |
| Duration Exceeds | The duration in minutes that a metric must be continuously triggered. A scale-out occurs if the average per-minute value of a metric consistently meets the threshold for this duration. Configure this setting based on the required sensitivity of your cluster service. |

anagement for ECS clusters

| Application Source | Note The Application Source feature is disabled by default. Contact an O&M engineer to enable this feature. Existing Resources: Uses a specified number of idle ECS instances from the application's current cluster for the scale-out. Note If the number of available ECS instances in the cluster is insufficient for the scale- out, EDAS uses the instances that are available. Elastic Resources: Purchases new instances based on an existing instance type or a launch template. These instances are then automatically imported into the cluster for the scale-out. Existing Resources First: Prioritizes idle instances in the cluster for scale-outs. If idle instances are insufficient, Auto Scaling purchases new instances. |
|---|---|
| Creation Method | Note This parameter appears when you set Application Source to Elastic Resources or Existing Resources First. Purchase Based On Existing Instance Type: Select an existing instance type from the cluster to use as a template for purchasing new instances. |
| Template Host | Note This parameter appears when you set Application Source to Elastic Resources or Existing Resources First. Select a launch template to use as a template for purchasing new instances. |

anagement for ECS clusters

| Logon Password | This parameter appears when you set Application Source to Elastic Resources or Existing Resources First. |
|---|---|
| Instances Per Scale-out | The number of instances that are automatically added each time a scale-out operation is triggered. |
| Maximum Instances In Group | When the number of servers in the cluster reaches the configured maximum, scaling out stops. Configure this value based on your resource quota. |

**View the Auto Scaling result**

After you configure the scaling rules, you can view the results of any automatic scale-out or scale-in operations in the following ways: On the **Basic Information** page of the application, check if the number of instances has changed. In the navigation pane on the left of the application details page, click **Change History**. For a change record where the **Change Type** is Scale Out or **Scale In** and the source is
**auto_scale**, click **View** in the **Actions** column to view the details.

#### Throttling and degradation

Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) supports throttling and degradation for Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and High-speed Service Framework (HSF) applications using Application High Availability Service (AHAS). EDAS lets you view throttling and degradation details and change rules in real time to ensure the availability of your applications.

**Prerequisites**

Your application is integrated with AHAS using the SDK. For more information, see the **AHAS**
**User Guide**.

**Background information**

By default, newly deployed applications use the AHAS component for throttling and degradation. To use this feature, enable AHAS when you create or deploy an application. For existing applications that do not use throttling and degradation, you can enable AHAS when you redeploy them to use this feature. For existing applications that already use throttling and degradation, the original implementation is retained.

**Overview of throttling and degradation**

Throttling Throttling controls traffic by setting thresholds or adjusting traffic ratios. If a frontend website receives high traffic, you can set a traffic threshold to control the maximum traffic that passes through the system. This prevents high traffic from overwhelming backend core systems and causing service outages, which ensures that the system runs securely and reliably. anagement for ECS clusters To enable throttling for a service provider, you must configure the throttling module on the provider side and configure a throttling policy in EDAS. When a service consumer calls the provider, the throttling module processes all requests. The throttling policy is triggered if the number of calls exceeds the preset threshold within a specific period.

| Number of calls exceeds Throt threshold (Throttled) Service Consumer A Normal call Service Consumer B | Throt | tlingModule Service Prov |
|---|---|---|
| Service Con |   |   |

| Service Con | Number of calls exceeds threshold (Throttled) sumer A |
|---|---|

Degradation In EDAS, degradation lowers the call priority of non-core downstream service providers when they time out. This ensures that upstream core applications, which are the service consumers, are not affected. To enable degradation for a service consumer, you must configure the degradation module on the consumer side and configure a degradation policy in EDAS. When the consumer calls a service provider, the degradation policy is triggered if the provider's response time exceeds the preset threshold.

| Service Con | Degra |
|---|---|

Call timeout DegradationModule (Degraded) Service Prov Normal call Service Prov

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
anagement for ECS clusters
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Throttling and Degradation**, and then select a
feature from the menu that appears. AHAS provides the following throttling and degradation features:
**API Details**: Displays metrics for all APIs of the application, such as passed queries per
second (QPS), throttled QPS, abnormal QPS, response time (RT), and concurrency data. You can also manage throttling rules for APIs on this page. For more information, see
**AHAS User Guide > API Details**.
**Machine Monitoring**: Displays metrics for all nodes, such as passed QPS, throttled QPS,
abnormal QPS, response time (RT), and concurrency. You can also manage throttling rules for APIs on this page. For more information, see **AHAS User Guide > Machine**
**Monitoring**.
**Rule Settings**: Displays information about the interfaces that are subject to rules such
as throttling, fencing, and degradation. You can also use this page to manage throttling rules for each interface. For more information, see **AHAS User Guide > Configure**
**Rules**.
**Operation Logs**: Records operations performed on applications by the current Alibaba
Cloud account and its RAM users. The logs include details such as resource names, operation content, operation times, and operator IDs. This lets you track changes to applications and resources. For more information, see **AHAS User Guide > Operation**
**Logs**.

#### Upgrade or downgrade the runtime

**environment**

After you deploy an application in an ECS cluster, you can upgrade or downgrade its runtime environment (EDAS Container) during operation and maintenance (O&M) to meet different functional requirements. This topic describes how to upgrade and downgrade the runtime environment of an application in EDAS.

**Application runtime environment**

Spring Cloud, Dubbo, and High-speed Service Framework (HSF) applications can be deployed in ECS clusters using WAR or JAR packages. The required runtime environment varies based on the application and package type.
**Native Applications Deployed by Using a WAR Package** : For Spring Cloud, Dubbo,
standard Java Web, or Spring MVC applications that do not use Pandora or Pandora Boot, you must select a compatible version of the Apache Tomcat runtime environment.
**Native Applications Deployed by Using JAR Packages** : For Spring Cloud, Dubbo,
standard Java Web, or Spring MVC applications that do not use Pandora or Pandora Boot, you must select the standard Java application runtime environment.
**HSF Applications**: For HSF applications, including Spring Cloud applications developed
with Pandora Boot and applications converted from Dubbo to HSF, you must select a compatible version of the EDAS-Container runtime environment when you deploy them using a WAR or JAR package.

**Upgrade or downgrade the runtime environment**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
anagement for ECS clusters
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. On the application's **Basic Information** page, in the upper-right corner, click
**Upgrade/Downgrade Runtime Environment**.
5. In the **Upgrade/Downgrade Runtime Environment** dialog box, select the runtime
environment version that you want to upgrade or downgrade, select **Java Environment**, and then click **OK**. Upgrade or downgrade the runtime environment for HSF applications. anagement for ECS clusters Upgrade or downgrade the runtime environment for Spring Cloud and Dubbo applications. This example uses an application deployed using a JAR package.

**Note**

You do not need to restart the application after the runtime environment is upgraded or downgraded. After the runtime environment is upgraded or downgraded, the application may become unavailable due to feature compatibility issues. Therefore, upgrade the runtime environment during off-peak hours, such as in the early morning.
6. Return to the **Basic Information** page and view the application runtime environment
version in the Application Information area. If the upgrade is successful, the target version is displayed. If the upgrade fails, a change log is generated. For more information, see Troubleshooting guide for change processes. If necessary, contact the EDAS helpdesk or roll back the application runtime environment to the original version.

##### Configure JVM parameters

You can configure Java Virtual Machine (JVM) parameters to enable the container parameter setting when an application is started. Specified valid JVM parameters help reduce the overhead of GC. This shortens the server response time and improves throughput.

**Background information**

anagement for ECS clusters

**g**

If you do not set custom JVM parameters, the JVM allocates default values. The configured JVM parameters take effect only after you restart the application.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the EDAS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Management > Applications**.
3. On the **Applications** page, select a region from the top menu bar. At the top of the page,
select the **Microservices Namespace**. From the **Cluster Type** drop-down list, select **ECS**
**Cluster**. In the **Applications** list, click the name of the target application.
4. On the **Basic Information** page, in the **Application Settings** section, select **Default JVM**
**Parameters (can be set separately for instance groups)** and click **Edit**.
5. In the **Default Application Settings (Can be set separately for instance groups)**
dialog box, expand **Memory Configuration**, **GC Policy**, **Tools**, and **Custom**, and set the related parameters. Then, click **Configure JVM Parameters**.

**Note**

You can hover the pointer over the icon next to a parameter to view its description. The JVM parameter settings are written to the bin/setenv.sh file in the container directory. You must restart the application for the settings to take effect.

| Configuration Item | Description |

A custom path is not required. The default path is /. Select Custom and enter a custom access path. If you do not set this parameter, the name of the WAR package is used by default. |
